identifier: Entity selection for transactions: POS
statement: For POS transactions, the physical location where the POS device is logged in determines the entity. Each POS location maps to a specific business entity during setup, and staff can't manually change the entity during checkout. The entity must be in the same country as the POS location.

identifier: Managing the business entity and Shopify Payments account connected to a region market
statement: You can connect any of your business entities to process transactions for online and retail sales, including multiple entities within the same country. For example, if you have business entities in Australia and the United States, then you can create regional markets for each country to ensure the domestic entity processes the sales. If you have multiple entities in the same country, such as separate online and retail entities, then you can assign each to the appropriate market.

identifier: Set up separate entities for each country with retail locations
statement: To manage retail businesses across multiple regions, you must have a separate entity for each country with retail locations, including pop-up locations.

identifier: Understanding customer privacy settings in your Shopify Admin: region picker cards
statement: When you log in to your Shopify admin, you can set up a privacy policy, add a cookie banner, allow visitors to opt-out of their data being sold or shared, update your Shopify Network Intelligence settings, and view information about the geographic storage location of your data. Your setting for Shopify Network Intelligence takes effect globally, but your settings for cookie banners and data sharing can be managed per region. The region picker cards, which include a dialog listing all available countries and states, are used for configuring where the consent banner and opt-out page are displayed in your online store. These cards display the regions currently selected based on your configured markets.

identifier: Add a cookie banner {#add-a-cookie-banner}: automated settings, Regions and content
statement: When you set up a new store, automated privacy settings are activated by default, which means we will automatically configure your cookie banner for visitors in the UK and EEA regions, if you have active markets in these regions. However, you can deactivate Use automated settings to manually draft your cookie banner. The Shopify cookie banner may be displayed on storefront, cart, and checkout and customer account pages to visitors in configured regions. Steps: 1. From your Shopify admin, go to Settings > Customer privacy. 2. Click Cookie banner. 3. In the Regions and content section, choose between automated settings or manual customization: * To use automated settings, make sure that the Use automated settings button is activated. If it's not, then activate it using the toggle. This option ensures that your settings remain aligned with Shopify's latest recommendations for regions and content. * For manual region customization, click Edit in the Regions section, select the regions where the cookie banner should display, click Done, and then click Save.

identifier: General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)
statement: The European Union's General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) imposes obligations and responsibilities with respect to personal data for businesses located in or offering goods or services to individuals in the European Economic Area, and Switzerland and the United Kingdom have adopted equivalent laws for UK and Swiss businesses and residents. By using Shopify, there are tools and information that you can use to help you to analyze your business practices and help ensure that you comply with your GDPR obligations. Using services offered by Shopify alone doesn't guarantee that you comply with GDPR. You're generally the controller of your customers’ data. This means that you choose how your customers’ data is handled. If you make goods and services available to individuals in Europe, even if you or your business aren't located in Europe, then GDPR might apply to your business.

identifier: Restrict access to your online store: private mode
statement: You can manage access to your online store by activating or deactivating private mode. In private mode, all of your online store's pages are hidden from visitors and search engines, and your online store displays a customizable landing page instead. Your store's landing page has a password, which you can share with visitors to allow them to access your online store when private mode is active.

identifier: Restrict access to your online store: store access when you first register for a Shopify plan
statement: When you first register for a Shopify plan, your store access is restricted to private mode by default. After you complete the required setup steps, you can launch your store to change access to public.

identifier: Restrict access to your online store: access setting menu (Online Store page) and Online Store > Preferences
statement: You can change your access mode from the access setting menu on the Online Store page of your Shopify admin, and manage additional private mode settings, such as your password, from the Online Store > Preferences page.

identifier: Manage private mode preferences {#add-password-protection-to-your-online-store}
statement: You can activate private mode for your online store, select a password that visitors can use to access your store, and optionally add a custom message to your store's password page from the Online Store > Preferences page of your Shopify admin.

identifier: Manage private mode preferences: Restrict access to B2B customers only
statement: Optional: Select Restrict access to B2B customers only to limit your store's access to B2B customers.

identifier: Manage private mode preferences, Mobile: Note (trial plan, business address)
statement: If your store is on a trial plan, or doesn't have a business address yet, then the Shopify app prompts you to complete that step before you can remove your password.

identifier: Customizing your password page template: Password page
statement: The Password page is the landing page displayed when a customer visits your website and private mode is active on your online store.

identifier: OnlineStorePasswordProtection.enabled (Admin GraphQL API 2026-10; QueryRoot.onlineStore, OnlineStore.passwordProtection)
statement: enabled Whether the storefront password is enabled.

identifier: Store settings permissions: Manage settings
statement: Manage settings This permission allows users to access some pages of the administration options on the Settings section and Preferences page of your Shopify admin, and to create webhooks.

identifier: Pixels overview: Shopify pixels manager, Customer events
statement: You can use the Shopify pixels manager to manage and add pixels that track customer events. Customer events are actions that take place in the customer's browser, for example, clicking a link or adding a product to a cart. You can add and manage pixels in the Customer events section of your Shopify admin.

identifier: Pixels overview: app pixels and custom pixels
statement: Pixels can be added to your online store in 2 ways: through app pixels, which are installed through marketing and data collection apps, and custom pixels, which can be manually added by a developer in the pixels manager of your Shopify admin.

identifier: Pixels overview: where pixels load
statement: Pixels automatically load on the Storefront, Checkout, Thank you page, and Order status page.

identifier: Pixels overview, Customer privacy {#customer-privacy}: markets configured to require consent
statement: In markets configured to require consent (usually the European Economic Area (EEA) and the United Kingdom), web pixels run only when visitors have provided the permissions required in the pixel configuration. By default, new pixels require Marketing and Analytics permissions.

identifier: Pixels overview, Customer privacy {#customer-privacy}: pixels configured as data sale
statement: Similarly, pixels configured as data sale won't run for customers that have opted out of data sales or sharing, unless the pixel supports limited data use.

identifier: Store settings permissions: View customer events
statement: View customer events This permission allows users to view customer events, including app pixels and custom pixels.

identifier: Store settings permissions: Manage and add custom pixels
statement: Manage and add custom pixels This permission allows users to manage and add custom pixels.

identifier: WebPixel (Admin GraphQL API 2026-10)
statement: The `WebPixel` object enables you to manage JavaScript code snippets that run on an online store and collect [behavioral data](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/web-pixels-api/standard-events) for marketing campaign optimization and analytics.

identifier: WebPixel.settings (Admin GraphQL API 2026-10)
statement: for the web pixel. This object specifies configuration options that control the web pixel's functionality and behavior.

identifier: Selling on Google AI Mode and Gemini: Google Analytics and custom pixels in direct checkout
statement: Google Analytics and custom pixels won't fire in Google AI Mode and Gemini's direct checkout. The checkout fires only server-to-server pixels (started, completed), so none of the standard or custom client side pixels fire.
scope: Google AI Mode and Gemini channel

identifier: Selling on Meta: Google Analytics and custom pixels in direct checkout
statement: Google Analytics and custom pixels won't fire in Meta's direct checkout. The checkout fires only server-to-server pixels (started, completed), so none of the standard or custom client side pixels fire.

identifier: Selling on Microsoft Copilot: Google Analytics and custom pixels in direct checkout
statement: Google Analytics and custom pixels won't fire in Microsoft Copilot's direct checkout. The checkout fires only server-to-server pixels (started, completed), so none of the standard or custom client side pixels fire.

identifier: Setting up staff notifications: Note
statement: Account owners receive notifications on all new orders by default. This can be deactivated by going to Settings > Notifications > Staff notifications.

identifier: Setting up staff notifications: events
statement: You can create and edit email notifications to let you or staff know when the following events occur in your Shopify admin: * Store order summary: A summary of your store orders, sales, and top products for the week. Sent by default every Monday at 9AM in your local timezone. You can specify the day and time in your notification settings, and you can set it to daily instead and choose the time. Recipients with this staff notification activated receive the notification regardless of their order or location permissions. * New order: Sent when a customer places an order. * New return request: Sent when a customer requests a return on an order. * Sales attribution ended: Sent to order notification recipients when the attributed staff on an order is edited. * New draft order: Sent when a customer submits a draft order. Only sent to the store owner. * Order dispute updates: Sent when a chargeback or inquiry is opened, escalated, reopened, won, lost, or prevented, and when evidence is submitted.

identifier: Setting up staff notifications: permissions
statement: You need the Orders and Manage settings permissions to make changes to order notifications.

identifier: Add a recipient for staff notifications: location
statement: Optional: If you have the POS sales channel installed and you want to create notifications for orders from a particular POS location or from the web, then select a location from the list. You can select All to create notifications for all orders. To add notifications for more than one specific location, you need to create them as separate order notifications.

identifier: Deactivate or reactivate staff notifications {#adjust-new-order-notifications}
statement: You can temporarily deactivate staff notifications instead of deleting the recipient. Afterward, you can reactivate the notifications.

identifier: Edit staff notifications sent to a recipient
statement: You can edit a recipient to only receive a staff notification for some staff notifications.

identifier: Store notifications: Notifications page
statement: You can manage email and SMS notifications that your store sends to customers and staff from the Notifications page in your Shopify admin. Notifications are triggered by specific events such as order placement, fulfillment, refunds, exchanges, and account changes.

identifier: Required store permissions for options on the Settings page: Notifications
statement: Notifications Allows you to manage the notifications that are sent to you and to your customers. Manage settings

identifier: Closing for vacations
statement: Although Shopify doesn't have a vacation setting, there are two ways that you can temporarily close your store to the general public, depending on how long you expect to be pausing sales.

identifier: Closing for vacations: Short-term solution: Activate private mode
statement: To temporarily stop visitors from accessing your store, activate private mode for your online store. Private mode means that without a password, customers can't do the following actions on your store: * Access your site * View products * View pages * Complete orders

identifier: Closing for vacations: Short-term solution: Activate private mode, charges
statement: When you restrict access to your store, your subscription charges and any other recurring charges continue as expected.

identifier: Closing for vacations: Long-term solution: Pause and Build
statement: The Pause and Build plan keeps your store online and accessible to visitors, but deactivates the following sales channels and purchase related features: * The online store checkout. * The Point of Sale channel. * Discounts. * Abandoned checkout recovery. * Gift cards. * Publish your products on third-party integrations, such as Facebook and Google.

identifier: Closing for vacations: Long-term solution: Pause and Build, subscription fee
statement: Selecting the Pause and Build plan changes your subscription fee to $9 USD per month. However, when you decide to unpause, you must select a new plan, as your old plan is no longer valid.

identifier: Closing for vacations: Long-term solution: Pause and Build, Plan page
statement: You can pause your store on the Plan page in the Settings section of your Shopify admin.

identifier: Closing for vacations: Long-term solution: Pause and Build, effective date
statement: When you switch to the Pause and Build plan, the change might be scheduled to take effect at the end of your current billing cycle, and the Shopify admin might display a future effective date. If you need to stop customers from placing orders before the change takes effect, then activate private mode in the meantime.

identifier: Pausing your store: Pause and Build plan
statement: If you want to take a pause from selling on Shopify temporarily, but continue working on your store, then you can use the Pause and Build plan. After you switch to the Pause and Build plan, your checkout is deactivated across all sales channels, such as the Point of Sale channel.

identifier: Considerations for pausing your store {#considerations-for-pausing}: requirements to select the Pause and Build plan
statement: Your store must meet the following requirements to select the Pause and Build plan: * You must be the store owner. * Your store needs to be past the free trial period. * Your store needs to be on a paid plan.

identifier: Launch your store {#remove-your-online-store-password}: private mode during your free trial
statement: During your free trial, your online store is automatically in private mode. In private mode, your site's pages are inaccessible, and a customizable landing page with a password option is displayed instead.

identifier: Launch your store {#remove-your-online-store-password}: required steps
statement: Before you can launch your store, you must complete the following required steps: * Select a subscription plan. If you pick a plan during a free trial, then you won't be charged any subscription fees until your free trial expires. * Add a store address to the Business details section of the Settings > General page. * Set up a payment method, and make sure that test mode is deactivated.

identifier: Activate push notifications {#activate-push-notifications} (Shopify app)
statement: You can set up push notifications in the Shopify app to get instant alerts on your phone about the following important store updates: * Critical alerts * Fulfillments * New orders * Setup tips * Timeline mentions

identifier: Activate push notifications {#activate-push-notifications}: Note
statement: When you activate notifications in the Shopify app, make sure to activate notifications in the main settings of your device.

identifier: Manage customer privacy settings {#customer-privacy} (custom pixels)
statement: You can manage the customer privacy settings for each of the custom pixels on your store. Your customer privacy settings determine when Pixels collects data, and for which purposes.

identifier: Manage customer privacy settings {#customer-privacy}: Permission setting (custom pixels)
statement: The Permission setting lets you determine whether customer permission is required under applicable laws for your custom pixel to collect data for marketing, analytics, and preferences purposes. To request customer consent to collect data based on your Permission setting, you need to add a cookie banner to your store.

identifier: Manage customer privacy settings {#customer-privacy}: Data sale setting (custom pixels)
statement: The Data sale setting lets you manage how your custom pixel collects data in cases where the customer has opted out of their data being sold, as provided for in certain jurisdictions.

identifier: App pixel permissions and customer privacy settings {#permissions-customer-privacy}: Staff permissions
statement: To manage app pixels, you need the Manage and install apps and channels permission in the Shopify admin.

identifier: App pixel permissions and customer privacy settings {#permissions-customer-privacy}
statement: When you install an app that has app pixels, it's your responsibility to ensure you're following applicable laws and to set up the appropriate privacy configuration, including consent and data sale opt-out options, to the extent that's required.

identifier: View permissions and customer privacy settings {#view-permissions} (app pixels)
statement: You can view a full list of the permissions and customer privacy settings that an app or sales channel has access to. The permissions and customer privacy settings for each app pixel are determined by the third-party app partner, and can't be changed.

identifier: Optimizing data access for app pixels {#optimize-data-access}: data access types
statement: You can choose how you want your pixel's customer and business data to be shared between your online store and your apps. There are 2 possible data access types for app pixels: - Always on: The app pixel has access to all of your customer and business data, without limitations. - Optimized: Shopify intelligently allows data access for optimal analytics and campaign performance.

identifier: Optimizing data access for app pixels {#optimize-data-access}: Note
statement: Optimization is supported for marketing pixels. Some types of app pixels, such as those from analytics apps, can't be optimized and retain Always on data access.

identifier: Change data access settings for app pixels {#change-data-access}
statement: By default, your app pixel's data access setting is Optimized. You can change the data access settings of an app pixel between Always on and Optimized at any time.

identifier: Viewing stores: Store status (Organization settings, Stores)
statement: A store's status is either active or pending Shopify Plus contract addition. By default, only active stores are displayed in the Stores section of the Organization settings. To review pending stores, click Pending.

identifier: Viewing stores: Store status, Descriptions of store statuses (Active; Pending contract addition)
statement: Active Active stores are fully activated stores. An active store isn't necessarily open to the public. Some setup for a new store might be required, such as adding products, staff, or sales channels. Pending contract addition Pending stores are newly created stores that might exceed your contract limits. Pending stores become active after the request has been processed by Shopify and you've approved any additional charges.

identifier: Trying Shopify with a free trial: private mode or inactive checkout
statement: When you open a store on a free trial, your store is initially in private mode, or its checkout is inactive.

identifier: Trying Shopify with a free trial: allowing customers to purchase products
statement: To allow customers to purchase products, you can either deactivate private mode, or you can activate your online store checkout, and POS in-person sales if applicable, by choosing a paid plan.

identifier: Trying Shopify with a free trial: Settings page (subscription plan, store type, store status)
statement: From the Settings page in your Shopify admin, you can manage your Shopify subscription plan, store type, and store status.

identifier: Frozen stores after missed bill payments
statement: If you missed paying your Shopify subscription bill, or if a payment fails multiple times, then your store is frozen until you settle your bill with Shopify. Your store doesn't freeze until your bill's due date. If your store is frozen, then you can't access your Shopify admin and customers can't view your store.

identifier: Setting your online store preferences: Manage store access settings {#add-or-remove-the-password-page}
statement: You can control whether visitors and search engines can access your online store from the Store access section of the Preferences page.

identifier: Setting your online store preferences: Manage store access settings, Private mode setting
statement: To restrict visitors and search engines from accessing your online store, activate the Private mode setting. When private mode is active, a landing page with a password option and a custom message is displayed to your visitors. To permit specific customers to access your online store when private mode is active, provide them with the password to bypass private mode.

identifier: Deactivating and reactivating your Shopify store
statement: If you're the store owner and your store is eligible, then you can use your Shopify admin to cancel your subscription and deactivate your store completely at the end of your current billing cycle.

identifier: Restrict access to your store or specific pages for B2B customers only {#restrict-access}
statement: By default, your B2B store is publicly accessible. Anyone can visit and browse your products and store content, including D2C customers. However, only logged-in B2B customers can access B2B-specific pricing, B2B-only products, and B2B-exclusive store content. If you operate a dedicated B2B store, then you can restrict access so that only logged-in B2B customers can view your store.

identifier: Considerations for restricting store access: blended store with B2B Markets
statement: If you operate a blended store with B2B Markets and customer accounts, then restricting access might redirect D2C customers to authentication on some pages. Test your storefront as both a B2B and D2C customer before activating this setting.

identifier: Order dispute updates {#order-dispute-updates} (staff notification)
statement: The Order dispute updates notification controls who receives email about chargebacks and inquiries. A staff member receives these emails only when both of the following are true: * They have the Disputes > Manage permission. * Order dispute updates is turned on for them in Settings > Notifications > Staff notifications.

identifier: Order dispute updates {#order-dispute-updates}: whole store or individual recipients
statement: You can turn the notification off for your whole store, or for individual recipients.

identifier: Customize the timing and frequency of your Store order summary
statement: By default, the Store order summary notification is set as weekly every Monday at 9AM in your local time. You can update the Store order summary to send on a different day or time, and you can set it to daily.

identifier: Set up notifications in Shopify Inbox
statement: When a customer starts a conversation, or replies to an existing conversation on your online store, you can be notified of their message through any of the following types of notifications: * Desktop notifications that are displayed in your browser to notify you that you have a new message. * Mobile notifications that display on the mobile devices that have the Shopify Inbox mobile app installed. * Email notifications that are sent to email accounts of Shopify users that have access to Shopify Inbox.

identifier: Set up notifications in Shopify Inbox: multiple stores
statement: If you have Inbox installed on multiple stores, then you receive notifications for each store that you're logged in to. To stop notifications for a single store, log out of that store from the side menu on mobile or the store dropdown on desktop.

identifier: Set up notifications in Shopify Inbox: Note
statement: You can manage notifications only for yourself. You can't change notification settings for other staff members. Unless a conversation is assigned to a staff member, all staff members are notified of new messages.

identifier: Send internal email (Shopify Flow action)
statement: Because variables can't be used to customize the address an email is sent to, the Send internal email action is best used to send emails to staff. To automate emails to customers, create a marketing automation.

identifier: Examples of workflows in Shopify Flow: Buyer experience workflows (internal notifications)
statement: Buyer experience workflows can add tags to your customers' orders or send internal notifications to help you learn more about their experience purchasing from your store.

identifier: Google Analytics
statement: If the questions you have about your store's performance can't be answered with the data available in Shopify's analytics, then you can use Google Analytics. Google Analytics lets you track visitors, sessions, and other customer behavior on your store.

identifier: Setting up Google Analytics 4
statement: Before you can start gathering data about your store, you need to have a Google Analytics account and create a Google Analytics 4 property. You can then set up Google Analytics 4 tags on your Shopify store, and link your Google Ads account to your Google Analytics account.

identifier: Setting up Google Analytics 4: Google & YouTube channel
statement: If you don't have the Google & YouTube channel installed, then you're prompted to install it during the set up process for your GA4 tags. You don't have to connect to the Google Merchant Center to complete your GA4 tags setup process.

identifier: Setting up Google Analytics 4: Note (private mode)
statement: Google Analytics can't track events until you deactivate private mode for your online store.

identifier: Custom pixels: Caution
statement: Custom pixels is an advanced feature that requires JavaScript knowledge. Compliance with applicable laws, consents, code security, troubleshooting, and updates are your responsibility. Pixels are subject to the Shopify Terms of Service.

identifier: Meta pixel: customer data-sharing level
statement: When you set up Facebook and Instagram by Meta, you can add a pixel to track customer data and behavior on your Online Store. To use a Meta pixel, you need to set a customer data-sharing level. It's up to you to decide how much data you want to track using the pixel. The Standard data sharing setting sends only customer behavior. The Enhanced and Maximum settings send additional customer information including name, location, and email address.

identifier: Facebook data sharing: Data sharing settings in Facebook and Instagram by Meta
statement: The Data sharing settings in Facebook and Instagram by Meta lets you choose how customer data and browsing behavior is collected in your online store.

identifier: Understanding customer privacy settings in your Shopify Admin: Google Consent Mode v2
statement: Google Consent Mode v2 is a feature that works with Google tags to handle user consent. Any event data transmitted to Google from customers, such as those located in the European Economic Area (EEA), won't be used for personalized advertising unless Google Consent Mode v2 is activated and valid consent is obtained.

identifier: Marketing app data sharing: Note
statement: Before marketing data is shared to Shopify, it's first checked against your privacy settings. If a customer opts out of data collection for your store, then their data isn't processed.

identifier: Understanding the impact of privacy setting {#analytics-cookies}
statement: Implementing cookie banners and data sharing opt-out features can affect data collection: * In configured cookie banner regions: Non-essential data is collected only after obtaining consent, which might reduce data available for analytics, marketing, and personalization. For example, this can be observed through decreased session counts and other metrics that rely on session data, including conversion rates. This is intended for use in regions that require opt-in consent for data collection, such as in the EEA and the UK. * Outside of UK, EEA, and other configured cookie banner regions: The cookie banner will not be active in these regions by default. This is intended for use in regions that don't require opt-in consent for cookies-based data collection, such as in the US. However, you can choose to use the cookie banner in any region. * Default settings: Automated privacy settings are on by default when you set up a new store. When automated privacy settings are enabled, the cookie banner is on by default if required by your currently active markets.

identifier: Understanding the impact of privacy setting {#analytics-cookies}: Pixels
statement: Pixels operate based on the consent obtained in these regions.

identifier: Manage store details {#manage-details} (Settings > General > Store contact details)
statement: You can update your store's name, email address, and phone number. This information is public, and your customers might view this information in your store and policies. The email address that you provide is the email address that customers can use to contact you. You must provide an email address in the Store contact details section.

identifier: Manage store details {#manage-details}: store phone number
statement: You can also choose to add a phone number for customers to provide additional customer service. This setting is optional.

identifier: Manage store details {#manage-details}, Steps: the Store contact details page
statement: On the Store contact details page, edit your store name, store email, or store phone number.

identifier: Set or change your store name and contact information {#online-store-and-legal-name}
statement: Store contact information is public. Customers can view this information on your store and policy pages. You can choose to share information such as your phone number with customers to provide customer service.

identifier: Set or change your store name and contact information {#online-store-and-legal-name}: changes
statement: If your store uses Shopify Payments, then you also need to contact Shopify Support to change the business name on your Shopify Payments account. Otherwise, there are no limits to changing your store name and contact information. You can change them as often as you want, at any time.

identifier: Adding store policies: the policies (Settings > Policies)
statement: You can manage the following policies for your Shopify store: * Return policy * Privacy policy * Terms of service * Shipping policy * Legal notice * Contact information * Subscription policy

identifier: Automated store policies {#automated-store-policies}
statement: Automated store policies use information from your store settings to generate and publish policy content, and keep that content updated when relevant settings change. You can manage automation separately for your return and refund policy, terms of service, shipping policy, and contact information.

identifier: Liquid variables used in automated store policies and their source settings: address (Contact information)
statement: address Contact information Your store address, formatted for the policy's language. Settings > General > Store contact details > Store address.

identifier: Liquid variables used in automated store policies and their source settings: legal_business_name, phone_number (Contact information)
statement: legal_business_name Contact information Your company name. If you don't enter a company name, then your store name is used. The company name in Settings > General > Store contact details > Store address. phone_number Contact information Your store phone number. Settings > General > Store contact details.

identifier: Liquid variables used in automated store policies and their source settings: store_name, support_contact (Contact information)
statement: store_name Contact information Your store name, when it differs from the company name displayed in the policy. Settings > General > Store contact details. support_contact Contact information The email address customers can use to contact you. Your Store email in Settings > General.

identifier: Liquid variables used in automated store policies and their source settings: vat_number (Contact information)
statement: vat_number Contact information Your European Union or United Kingdom VAT registration number. Your tax registrations in Settings > Taxes and duties. If you have several eligible registrations, then the first one added is used. Import One-Stop Shop (IOSS) numbers aren't used.

identifier: Review policies in your store's languages {#fr-it-sp-policies}
statement: If you sell in multiple languages, then review the policy content available to customers in each language. Make sure that translated policies accurately reflect your business practices and the commitments in your default-language policy.

identifier: Consumer protection laws: Contact information (under the Shopify Terms of Service)
statement: Under the Shopify Terms of Service, you must provide current and accurate contact information on your online store. This information must include: * your business name * an email address and a phone number customers can use to contact you with any questions, complaints, or claims * the physical address for your business

identifier: Consumer protection laws: Contact information, where to show it
statement: Your contact information needs to be public-facing and easy to access. You can add store policies, or you can add a Contact Us page to your online store.

identifier: Contact information requirements by the European Economic Area
statement: If you're a merchant located in, or shipping to, the European Economic Area, or if you're a merchant targeting consumers in the European Economic Area, then you're required to include your company number and Value-Added Tax (VAT) number on your online store.

identifier: Required legal notice for using Shopify Payments in Japan {#required-pages-for-using-shopify-payments-in-japan}
statement: If you use Shopify Payments in Japan, then you're required to have a legal notice containing information for the Specified Commercial Transactions Act (特定商取引法に基づく表記). Add this legal notice in the Legal notice section of Settings > Policies, and not as a page.

identifier: Add policies to your checkout page (Japan)
statement: Your store's terms of service, refund policy, shipping policy, and legal notice can be stored directly in the Policies page of your Shopify admin. Saved policies are automatically linked in the footer of your checkout.

identifier: Add policies to your checkout page, Steps (Japan): Contact information
statement: * Add your contact information in the Contact information section.

identifier: Display important information on the checkout page for Brazil: introduction
statement: Merchants who sell in Brazil often display links to the following information on their checkout page: * Legal notice, which displays information about your company (such as its name, address, and contact details)

identifier: Add policies to your checkout page, Steps (Brazil): Contact information
statement: * Add your legal notice to the Contact information box.

identifier: Display important information on the checkout page for France: introduction
statement: Merchants who sell in France often display links to the following information on their checkout page: * Legal notice, which displays information about your company (such as its name, address, and contact details)

identifier: Add policies to your checkout page, Steps (France): Contact information
statement: * Add your legal notice to the Contact information box.

identifier: Display important information on the checkout page for Germany: introduction
statement: Merchants who sell in Germany often display links to the following information on their checkout page: * Imprint, _Impressum_, or legal notice, which displays information about your company (such as its name, address, and contact details)

identifier: Add policies to your checkout page, Steps (Germany): Contact information
statement: * Add your legal notice to the Contact information box.

identifier: Display your store policies and other legal information (Italy; Spain): Note
statement: Displaying contact information is mandatory for merchants selling in the EU.

identifier: INFORM Consumers Act requirements {#requirements}: Display of seller information
statement: Display of seller information: For high-volume sellers with annual gross revenues of $20,000 USD or more on an online marketplace, the seller's business name, physical address, and contact information must be displayed on product listing pages, or in order confirmation messages and account transaction histories. Store contact information must include a working phone number, email address, or direct electronic messaging.
scope: Shop app; high-volume sellers who sell to customers in the United States

identifier: Edit your Shop Store details
statement: You can edit your store profile, avatar, and contact information in the Shop sales channel.

identifier: Edit your Shop Store details: contact information and social media links
statement: You can update the following contact information and social media links for your Shop Store: * Contact URL * Email address * Phone number * Business address * Social media links for Instagram, Facebook, Pinterest, YouTube, and Twitter

identifier: Google & YouTube channel requirements: contact information
statement: You need to add your contact information to a page in your online store, and the information needs to be visible to customers. You need to include at least one contact method such as email address, phone number, mailing address, or a contact form.

identifier: Configuring customer privacy settings: other store policies
statement: Automation for other store policies, such as your return and refund policy, shipping policy, and contact information, is managed separately in Settings > Policies.

identifier: Locations
statement: You can add and manage locations where you store or sell products, such as warehouses, retail stores, or pop-ups. A location is any physical place where you sell products, fulfill orders, or stock inventory. Some apps, including dropshipping apps and third-party logistics services, can also be considered locations.

identifier: Setting up and managing locations (Settings > Locations)
statement: You can add, deactivate, reactivate, and delete your locations from the Locations settings in your Shopify admin. You can also view, filter, sort, and search your locations in Settings > Locations > All locations. The maximum number of locations depends on your store's Shopify subscription plan.

identifier: Location quantity limit {#location-limit}: apps treated as locations
statement: If you use apps that physically stock inventory for you, then they're treated as locations. Inventory apps include dropshipping apps, third-party logistics services, and custom fulfillment services.

identifier: Add a location {#create-and-modify-locations}
statement: You can add a location in your Shopify admin. Your inventory is made available for online purchases by default in each new location. After you create a location, you can activate delivery methods for your location. Your new location is added to the bottom of your order routing list.

identifier: Add a location {#create-and-modify-locations}, Steps, step 4: online orders
statement: Optional: If you don't want to make your inventory available for online purchases at this location, then deactivate the Inventory at this location is available to fulfill online orders option. This option is activated by default for each new location.

identifier: Order routing (Settings > Shipping and delivery)
statement: You can set up order routing to automatically assign orders to fulfillment locations based on configured rules. Order routing applies rules in sequence to prioritize locations and determine where to fulfill each order. Order routing requires 2 or more active locations. The default order routing strategy includes rules to do the following: * Minimize split fulfillments by choosing locations that can fulfill all items * Stay within the destination market when possible * Ship from the closest location to reduce delivery times

identifier: Understanding order routing: default rules
statement: By default, rules are configured to optimize for fulfillment from the closest location within the destination market that has all of the items in the order in stock. There's no need to modify your order routing settings if the default settings work for your business.

identifier: Understanding order routing: rule Stay within the destination market
statement: Stay within the destination market Locations within the same market as the shipping address are prioritized.

identifier: Setting up order routing
statement: Order routing rules determine the locations to use to fulfill each item in a customer order. You can add, edit, remove, and rearrange order routing rules determine how locations are prioritized.

identifier: Manage the POS subscription plan for each location {#pos-pro-sub-management}
statement: If you're the account owner, then you can select your POS subscriptions by location to ensure that your stores have the subscription that best suits their needs.

identifier: Country and currency compliance for Shopify POS
statement: When you process a POS transaction in person using Shopify Payments and a Shopify card reader, you must follow the payment rules for the country you're processing the transaction in.

identifier: Setting up pickup in store for online orders: per location
statement: You can set up pickup in store for your locations. You need to set up pickup in store for each location where customers can pick up their orders.

identifier: Setting up order fulfillment for locations
statement: After you add locations, you need to configure how each location fulfills orders. When you have multiple active locations, online orders are assigned to locations based on available inventory and the order routing rules you configure.

identifier: Change the default location {#change-the-default-location}
statement: You can set any of your active locations to be the default location. Apps and deactivated locations can't be set as the default location. If you change the default location to a location where a carrier isn't supported, then the rates for that carrier are hidden at checkout. For example, if you set a default location in the United States, then Canada Post rates aren't displayed at checkout.

identifier: Setting up customer notifications
statement: Customer notifications are automated emails and SMS messages sent to customers about their orders, shipping updates, and account activity. Most customer notifications are sent automatically and can't be deactivated.

identifier: Setting up customer notifications: Shop app notifications (note headed Plan requirement)
statement: Notifications sent from the Shop app for tracking updates and order statuses can't be deactivated or edited by merchants. These notifications can only be turned off through a customer's Shop app settings.

identifier: Automatically email customers a link to complete their abandoned checkout {#automatically-email-checkout-link}
statement: You can automatically send an email to customers after they have abandoned their checkout. Each email contains a link to the customer's abandoned cart, allowing them to complete their checkout if they choose. You can edit the email template by adding a logo or changing the color scheme.

identifier: Automatically email customers a link to complete their abandoned checkout, Steps 1 to 3 (Apps > Messaging > Automations)
statement: 1. From your Shopify admin, go to Apps > Messaging. 2. Click Automations. 3. In the Abandoned checkout emails by Shopify automation, click > Edit settings.

identifier: Automatically email customers a link to complete their abandoned checkout, Steps 4 and 5 (Send to, Send after)
statement: 4. In the Abandoned checkout emails section, select Send abandoned checkout emails automatically. 5. Adjust the settings abandoned checkout email settings: 1. In the Send to section, select the category of visitor that you want to send abandoned checkout emails to. 2. In the Send after section, select how much time should pass from when the customer abandons their checkout to when the automated email sends.

identifier: Setting up SMS notifications
statement: You can give your customers the option of entering a phone number at checkout instead of an email address. If you have SMS notifications set up, and if your business address is in a supported country, then customers who enter a phone number instead of an email address will receive their order confirmation by SMS to their mobile phone.

identifier: Considerations about SMS Sender IDs: store name
statement: Your store's SMS Sender ID (the sender name displayed on SMS messages from your store) is based on your store name in your general Store contact details settings. There are restrictions to how your SMS Sender ID displays to your customers:

identifier: Considerations about SMS Sender IDs: countries and regions
statement: * Some countries and regions don't support dynamic SMS Sender IDs, in which case your store's numerical phone number displays as your SMS Sender ID instead.

identifier: Translating checkout and email notifications: published languages
statement: After you add and publish a language, the translated content is displayed in the checkout and in any email notifications sent to your customer.

identifier: Translating checkout and email notifications: the customer's language
statement: If translations are available for an email notification, then a customer is automatically sent email notifications in the language that they placed their order in. You can edit a customer profile to change the language of the notifications that a customer receives.

identifier: Add or edit an email notification translation (Translate & Adapt)
statement: You can add or edit email notification translations for the languages that you have added to your store using the Translate & Adapt app from Shopify.

identifier: Customizing email notification templates: sender email
statement: Before you can edit the body and the subject heading of your email notifications, you need to confirm your sender email address.

identifier: Changing the language of your email templates
statement: The default language that your email templates display in depends on your theme's language and any edits that you've made to the templates: * If you've made no changes to your email templates, then when you change your theme's language, the email template language also changes. * If you've made changes to both the body and title of your email templates, then changing your theme's language doesn't change the language of the email templates. * If you've made changes only to the title of your email templates, then changing your theme's language doesn't change the language of the email templates. * If you've made changes only to the body of your email templates, then changing your theme's language changes the title to the new language but doesn't change the language of the body of your email templates.

identifier: Add a tax registration number to the invoice: countries and regions
statement: In some countries and regions, you might need to include your tax registration number on customer invoices or other notices. In Australia, Canada, and India, businesses that charge the goods and services tax (GST) might need to include their registration number. In the European Union, you might need to include your value added tax (VAT) identification number.

identifier: Setting up your email: Sender email (Settings > Notifications)
statement: Your Sender email is the customer-facing address that's listed in Settings > Notifications and is used in the following ways: * As the email address where your customers can contact you directly. * As the From email address when your customers receive automatic notification emails, order confirmation emails, and any marketing emails sent from your store. * As the address where contact form submissions from your online store are delivered.

identifier: Store address compared to billing address (Settings > General > Store contact details)
statement: Your store address is the physical or customer-facing address of your business. Customers can view this address on your store and policy pages. You can manage it in the **Store contact details** section of the **Settings** > [**General**](https://admin.shopify.com/settings/general) page.

identifier: Email hosting and forwarding: store email addresses
statement: Email is an important tool for communicating with customers and sending notifications. You can increase trust in your business by providing one or more store email addresses where customers can send questions about products or orders.

identifier: Managing your Shopify account: the account's email and the store email
statement: This email address is used to contact you about your Shopify account, and is separate from the store email address that your customers use to contact you.

identifier: Best practices for writing marketing emails with Shopify Messaging: template branding and the store name
statement: By default, template branding matches the [**Brand**](https://admin.shopify.com/store/settings/general/branding) settings, and your store name from the **Store contact details** section of your [**General**](https://admin.shopify.com/settings/general) settings of your Shopify admin.

identifier: Printing shipping labels and shipping documents: phone numbers on labels
statement: Phone numbers for labels are taken from your location address in Settings > Locations. If no location phone number is provided, then the phone number from Settings > Store contact details is used.

statement: Set up or change your online store contact information, legal business name and address, store currency, and default weight units.

identifier: Retail markets overview and requirements: Currency, markets, and business entities {#currency-markets-and-business-entities}, One business entity
statement: One business entity: Shopify POS transactions process in your store’s default currency. Retail markets still control catalog and price rules for your retail locations, but they don’t change the processing currency for Shopify POS when you have a single entity.
scope: Shopify POS; stores with one business entity

identifier: Retail markets overview and requirements: Currency, markets, and business entities {#currency-markets-and-business-entities}, Multiple business entities
statement: Multiple business entities: The entity assigned to each retail location determines the currency for Shopify POS at that location, including how the location maps to its Retail market.
scope: Shopify POS; stores with multiple business entities

identifier: Retail markets overview and requirements: Currency, markets, and business entities {#currency-markets-and-business-entities}, in-person card payments in a country's local currency
statement: To process in-person card payments using integrated card readers in a country’s local currency, the entity for that location must use a default payout currency that matches the country and currency requirements for that country.

identifier: Retail markets overview and requirements: Shopify plan considerations for Retail markets, Shopify POS Lite
statement: Locations that are on Shopify POS Lite use Region markets only. You assign catalogs to a Region market to control which products are available and which prices apply in that region. Your retail locations and your online store in that region use the same catalog settings.

identifier: Retail markets overview and requirements: Shopify plan considerations for Retail markets, Region markets
statement: You can't apply different market settings to retail and online customers within the same region. Region markets apply in the same way to your online store and to retail locations in that region.

identifier: Setting up shipping options for a market: shipping rates by product or fulfillment location
statement: Each rate can apply to specific products or fulfillment locations, so you can charge different prices for different products or locations. By default, a rate applies to all products in the market.

identifier: Managing fulfillment locations in shipping profiles: Note (shipping options by market)
statement: Shipping profiles and shipping rates are gradually moving to shipping options by market, a new way to manage shipping from your markets. Most stores still use shipping profiles and shipping rates, and your store keeps its current setup until it's upgraded.

identifier: Country-specific retail requirements: cross-entity returns and exchanges
statement: In France, Spain, Italy, Germany, and Sweden, a return or exchange against an original sale must be processed by the same legal entity as the original sale to be compliant.
scope: Shopify POS in France, Spain, Italy, Germany and Sweden

identifier: Tax summaries and registration numbers for stores in Canada {#tax-summary-canada}
statement: Receipts include your GST/HST registration number for Canadian locations and your QST registration number for Québec locations.
scope: Shopify POS receipts; Canadian and Québec locations

identifier: Retail requirements in Spain {#spain}: product bundles
statement: You can't sell product bundles in Shopify POS for retail locations in Spain.

identifier: General tax set-up steps, step 1 (default location)
statement: Determine where you have an obligation to collect tax. This typically starts with your default location and where you operate your business from. This is usually your home country, province, or state.

identifier: Requirements for buying shipping labels {#ss-availability}
statement: To buy shipping labels in Shopify, your business needs to have an eligible fulfillment location and for some carriers your store needs to be based in the same country as the fulfillment location.

identifier: Requirements for buying shipping labels {#ss-availability}: Evri and DPD
statement: For example, if you want to buy shipping labels from Evri or DPD, then you need to have a fulfillment location in the United Kingdom and your store's address needs to be based in the United Kingdom.
scope: Evri and DPD shipping labels (United Kingdom)

identifier: Considerations for cash rounding on Shopify POS {#considerations-cash-rounding}
statement: Cash rounding applies only when the currency used at checkout matches the local currency of the retail location. You can configure the currency used at checkout with Retail markets.

identifier: Cash rounding rules {#cash-rounding-rules}
statement: Cash rounding rules might apply automatically at checkout depending on your store's location and when you opened your store in a particular country. Some rules apply to all stores in specific countries.

identifier: Cash rounding rules {#cash-rounding-rules}: new stores and first retail locations
statement: Starting July 26, 2026, additional rules apply to new stores created on or after July 6, 2026, and to existing stores that set up their first retail location in a listed country on or after July 6, 2026.

identifier: Charge tax on shipping rates
statement: The Charge tax on shipping rates setting affects only those countries and regions where tax is not automatically calculated. In the following countries and regions, shipping is taxed where applicable regardless of this setting:

identifier: Charge tax on shipping rates, the countries and regions where shipping is taxed regardless of the setting
statement: * Australia * Canada * the European Union * New Zealand * Norway * Switzerland * the United Kingdom * the United States

identifier: Charge tax on shipping rates, Steps
statement: 1. From your Shopify admin, go to Settings > Taxes and duties. 2. In the Global settings section, select Charge tax on shipping rates. 3. Click Save.

identifier: Activate duties and import tax collection
statement: You can manage the duty and import tax settings for your store in the Taxes and duties section of the Shopify admin. After the feature is activated, you can also manage the settings for collecting duty and import taxes for countries and regions in the Markets section of the Shopify admin.

identifier: Postal duty rates {#postal-rates}, Note
statement: When activated, postal duty rates apply to all international checkouts with the United States as the destination, regardless of the shipping options that are available to your customers. If you use a commercial carrier, then you cover the cost of any difference in incurred duties and import tax charged by customs authorities.
scope: postal duty rates, packages shipped to the United States

identifier: Determine duties for Section 232 tariffs {#232-tariffs}, considerations
statement: Review the following considerations before activating this feature: * The percentage that you select applies to the calculation of duties and import taxes only for shipments to locations in the United States. It doesn't apply to any other destination. * The percentage that you select applies to all products in your store that are subject to Section 232. You can't set different percentages for individual products. * The default percentage for the Section 232 setting is 100%. If you don't change this percentage, then tariffs are calculated assuming that your products that are subject to Section 232 are made of 100% steel or aluminum.
scope: Section 232 tariffs, shipments to locations in the United States

identifier: Considerations when selling from multiple entities with Shopify Payments
statement: Your main Shopify account is considered your primary entity, and other Shopify accounts that you add are considered your secondary entities. Certain features such as adding a third-party payment method are available only for the primary entity. Learn more about managing business entities.
scope: selling from multiple entities with Shopify Payments

identifier: Considerations when selling from multiple entities with Shopify Payments
statement: If a primary entity is using a third-party payment processor, then you can't add Shopify Payments to your secondary entity. To add Shopify Payments to a secondary entity, you must deactivate the third-party payment provider. Learn more about activating Shopify Payments. To use Shopify Payments alongside the third-party provider on the primary entity, learn more about using Shopify Payments with a third-party provider.
scope: selling from multiple entities with Shopify Payments

identifier: Considerations when selling from multiple entities with Shopify Payments
statement: You can offer subscription orders when you're selling from multiple entities with Shopify Payments, but all subscription payments are processed through your primary entity. International card fees and foreign exchange (FX) fees might apply depending on where your customer and your primary business entity are located. Learn more about currency conversion fees with Shopify Payments.
scope: selling from multiple entities with Shopify Payments

identifier: Considerations when selling from multiple entities with Shopify Payments
statement: Additional third-party payment methods are displayed only on checkouts and for markets associated with the primary entity, with the exception of PayPal.
scope: selling from multiple entities with Shopify Payments

identifier: Considerations when selling from multiple entities with Shopify Payments
statement: You can offer Shop Pay Installments on any of your entities that meet the Shop Pay Installments eligibility requirements, including secondary entities. Shop Pay Installments is activated and managed separately for each entity's Shopify Payments account. Newly added eligible entities might have Shop Pay Installments activated by default when Shopify Payments is activated.
scope: selling from multiple entities with Shopify Payments

identifier: Considerations when selling from multiple entities with Shopify Payments
statement: Post-purchase apps, such as cross-sell apps, might not work correctly with multi-entity setups. Purchases made through unsupported apps are routed to the primary entity, regardless of the customer's market. If you use post-purchase apps, then choose one of the following options: * Deactivate the app. * Configure the app to work only in markets served by the primary entity. * Manually reconcile your payouts.
scope: selling from multiple entities with Shopify Payments

identifier: Considerations when selling from multiple entities with Shopify Payments
statement: If you're using managed markets, then you can't sell from multiple entities with Shopify Payments.
scope: selling from multiple entities with Shopify Payments

identifier: Considerations when selling from multiple entities with Shopify Payments
statement: If you're using automated tax filing, then you can't sell from multiple entities with Shopify Payments.
scope: selling from multiple entities with Shopify Payments

identifier: Edit a business entity {#edit-entity}
statement: An entity can be assigned to multiple stores. Changes to an entity affect all stores that the entity is assigned to.

identifier: Set a store's default business entity {#set-business-entity}
statement: You can set a default business entity for a store from the Settings > General page of your Shopify admin.

identifier: Set a store's default business entity {#set-business-entity}
statement: If your store uses financial services such as Shopify Payments, Shopify Balance, Shopify Capital, or Shopify Credit, then you need to deactivate all financial services before you can switch business entities in your Shopify admin. Only the store owner can deactivate Shopify Payments.

identifier: Local payment methods, Caution
statement: To offer local payment methods in countries outside your business location, ensure those countries are set up as markets. Learn more about international payments.
scope: local payment methods with Shopify Payments

identifier: Local payment methods
statement: You can activate local payment methods with Shopify Payments to offer customers region-specific ways to pay at checkout. Each method is available only when a customer is in a supported country and selects an eligible currency. Orders paid using local payment methods are included in your Shopify Payments payouts alongside credit and debit card transactions.
scope: local payment methods with Shopify Payments

identifier: Shop Pay Installments account suspensions
statement: Shop Pay Installments is powered by Affirm. After you activate Shop Pay Installments, Affirm periodically reviews your online store to make sure that you're in compliance with their prohibited business policy. If you violate the policy, then a message stating that your Shop Pay Installments account is suspended displays in your admin.

identifier: Shop Pay Installments account suspensions, examples of reasons
statement: The following are examples of some of the reasons your Shop Pay Installments account can be suspended:

identifier: Shop Pay Installments account suspensions, examples of reasons
statement: * A password is required to access your online store. * The primary currency of your online store isn't USD, CAD, or GBP. * The primary language of your online store isn't English. * Your store doesn't have an online website. * Your business is primarily a Business-to-Business (B2B) service. * Your business involves gambling, financial services, or another category that Affirm doesn't support. * You're selling regulated products such as tobacco or drug paraphernalia. * You're selling prohibited products such as currencies or weapons.

identifier: 🚀 صفحة الأسواق المتعددة
statement: تحتوي صفحة الأسواق المتعددة على قائمة بالأسواق المُضافة ومعلومات حول كل سوق، أهمها: - المعلومات الأساسية حول السوق - العملات - الفروع والمستودعات - الشحن - معلومات التواصل - الدومين - خيارات الدخول والتسجيل - تصميم المتجر

identifier: القسم 1: المعلومات الأساسية
statement: اختر الدول التي سيُعرض لها السوق، واسم يدل على هذه السوق، بالإضافة للغة الافتراضية واللغات الأخرى المدعومة للسوق، وهل تريد إظهار السوق للعملاء أم لا.

identifier: القسم 1: المعلومات الأساسية
statement: 🔔 ملاحظة : يتم تحديد اللغة وتطبيقها بشكل مستقل لكل سوق.

identifier: القسم 3: الفروع والمستودعات
statement: 1. حدد الفروع الخاصة بالسوق، وخصص الخيارات الأخرى.

identifier: القسم 3: الفروع والمستودعات
statement: 2. حدد استراتيجية إنقاص المخزون: تحديد كيفية انقاص كميات المنتجات التي يتم شراؤها من الكميات المحددة للفروع , وتتضمن الخيارات التالية: - حسب الفرع/المستودع الأكثر كمية: تنقص الكمية من الفرع أو المستودع الذي تكون فيه كمية المنتج الأكبر من بقية المستودعات. - حسب الفرع/المستودع الأقرب للعميل: تنقص الكمية من الفرع أو المستودع الذي يكون الأقرب لموقع العميل. - حسب أولوية الفرع/المستودع: تنقص الكمية حسب ترتيب التاجر للفروع أو المستودعات.

identifier: القسم 3: الفروع والمستودعات
statement: 3. عرض حالة توفر المنتج تستطيع تفعيل خيار توفر المنتج في صفحة المنتج وذلك بعرض قائمة الفروع فقط مع حالة توفر المنتج : (متوفر - غير متوفر - كمية محدودة) مما يساعد العميل على اختيار الفرع المناسب عند الدفع واستلام المنتج من الفرع.

identifier: القسم 4: الشحن
statement: تنقسم إعدادات الشحن إلى أربعة أقسام، وهي: 1- تخصيص شحن منتجات الطلب الواحد من عدة فروع 2- حساب تكلفة الشحن 3- تخصيص الإسناد التلقائي لشركات الشحن 4- إصدار شحنات المنتجات غير محدودة الكمية من الفرع الافتراضي

identifier: القسم 5: معلومات التواصل
statement: امتثالاً لقوانين التجارة الإلكترونية يجب على كل متجر إضافة معلومات خدمة العملاء.

identifier: القسم 6: الدومين
statement: حدد الدومين الخاص بالسوق بإحدى طريقتين: أولاً: دومين فرعي مضاف مسبقاً ثانياً: دومين فرعي جديد

identifier: القسم 7: خيارات الدخول والتسجيل
statement: يمكنك من خلالها تفعيل طرق تسجيل الدخول والتسجيل لعملائك بسهولة. 1- التسجيل بالبريد الإلكتروني: من خلال إدخال البريد الإلكتروني وكلمة المرور. 2- التسجيل برقم الجوال (OTP): من خلال إرسال رمز تحقق إلى رقم جوال العميل المدخل.

identifier: القسم 8: تصميم المتجر
statement: سيأخذ السوق ثيم المتجر الرئيسي افتراضياً، ويمكنك إنشاء نسخة مخصصة للسوق أو اختيار ثيم جديد من متجر الثيمات بضغط (إدارة الثيمات).

identifier: القسم 8: تصميم المتجر
statement: يمكنك عند نشر ثيم ما تخصيصه لأسواق معينة.

identifier: 📍 استعراض وزيارة السوق
statement: 📝 ملاحظة: سيُعرض لك المتجر بالدومين الفرعي المخصص للسوق في حال إضافته، وإلا سيعرض المتجر بالدومين الأساسي للمتجر.

identifier: 🛍️ ترتيب المنتجات حسب الأسواق
statement: الآن يمكنك جعل متجرك يعكس ذوق واهتمام كل سوق على حدة من خلال ترتيب المنتجات داخل كل تصنيف بشكل مختلف بحسب السوق (الدولة).

identifier: ❓ هل إعداد اللغات من إعدادات المتجر ينطبق على جميع الأسواق؟
statement: ❓ هل إعداد اللغات من إعدادات المتجر ينطبق على جميع الأسواق؟ لا، ينطبق على السوق الافتراضي فقط. ويمكنك تحديد اللغات لكل سوق إضافي بشكل مستقل.

identifier: ❓ كيف أحدد اللغات للأسواق المتعددة في متجري؟
statement: من إعدادات كل سوق، يمكنك تحديد اللغات الخاصة به بشكل مستقل.

statement: في حال تم تفعيل ميزة الأسواق المتعددة ، ستظهر أيقونة اختيار السوق في صفحة طرق الدفع، حيث تتيح لك اختيار السوق الذي ترغب في إدارة إعداداته، والتنقل بسهولة بين الأسواق المختلفة المرتبطة بمتجرك.

identifier: - حدود الدفع الإلكتروني
statement: تتيح لك الاطلاع على الحدود المسموحة لعمليات الدفع الإلكتروني حسب الدولة ونوع المنتج لضمان عمليات دفع آمنة ومتوافقة مع السياسات المعتمدة.

identifier: ❓في حال تغعيل ميزة الأسواق المتعددة، كيف يمكنني التحكم بإخفاء وإظهار المنتج في سوق معين؟
statement: ❓في حال تغعيل ميزة الأسواق المتعددة، كيف يمكنني التحكم بإخفاء وإظهار المنتج في سوق معين؟ من صفحة بيانات المنتج، اضغط (المعلومات المتقدمة)، ومن خلال حقل (عرض المنتج في السوق) يمكنك إظهار المنتج في المتجر بإضافة اسم السوق المراد عرض المنتج به.

identifier: ❓ عند إلغاء التصنيف من المنتج، هل تؤثر على جميع الأسواق المتعددة؟
statement: ❓ عند إلغاء التصنيف من المنتج، هل تؤثر على جميع الأسواق المتعددة؟ نعم ، إزالة التصنيف من المنتج تؤدي تلقائيًا إلى إزالة المنتج من هذا التصنيف في جميع الأسواق المتعددة، ولا يمكن تخصيص ذلك لسوق معينة.

identifier: 💡 مثال 4 : رفض الطلبات التي لا يتطابق فيها رقم الهاتف مع دولة الشحن
statement: 💡 مثال 4 : رفض الطلبات التي لا يتطابق فيها رقم الهاتف مع دولة الشحن يمكنك استخدام قيد التحقق من تطابق رقم الهاتف مع دولة الشحن للتأكد من توافق بيانات العميل مع نطاق الشحن الذي يوفره متجرك.

identifier: 💡 مثال 5 : التحقق من تطابق دولة الشحن مع موقع العميل بناءً على عنوان IP
statement: 💡 مثال 5 : التحقق من تطابق دولة الشحن مع موقع العميل بناءً على عنوان IP يمكنك استخدام عنوان IP للتحقق من موقع العميل التقريبي ومقارنته بدولة الشحن المحددة في الطلب، للمساعدة في رصد بعض الطلبات التي قد تحتاج إلى تحقق إضافي.

identifier: 💡 مثال 6 : التحقق من تطابق دولة إصدار بطاقة الدفع مع دولة الشحن
statement: إذا كنت ترغب في التحقق من توافق دولة إصدار بطاقة الدفع مع دولة الشحن، يمكنك إعداد قيد يتعامل مع الطلبات التي تختلف فيها الدولتان وفقًا للإجراء الذي تحدده.

identifier: 💡 مثال 9 : تخصيص طرق دفع حسب السوق في المتاجر متعددة الأسواق
statement: 💡 مثال 9 : تخصيص طرق دفع حسب السوق في المتاجر متعددة الأسواق إذا كنت تستخدم ميزة الأسواق المتعددة في متجرك، يمكنك تخصيص طرق الدفع لكل سوق بما يتناسب مع خيارات الدفع التي ترغب في إتاحتها لعملائك في كل دولة.

identifier: خطوات إدارة أولوية العروض لكل سوق
statement: 1. من القائمة الرئيسية، اضغط اعدادات المتجر. 2. من قسم التسويق، اختر ( أولوية العروض ). 3. من فلتر (السوق)، اختر السوق الذي تريد إدارة عروضه. 4. رتّب العروض حسب الأولوية التي تناسب هذا السوق.

identifier: ❓هل تظهر أولوية العروض حسب السوق لجميع التجار؟
statement: ❓هل تظهر أولوية العروض حسب السوق لجميع التجار؟ تظهر إمكانية اختيار السوق وإدارة أولوية العروض بشكل مستقل للتجار الذين لديهم سوقان نشطان أو أكثر. أما إذا كان متجرك يعمل في سوق واحد فقط، فلن يظهر فلتر السوق، وتستمر إدارة أولوية العروض بالطريقة المعتادة.
scope: التجار الذين لديهم سوقان نشطان أو أكثر

identifier: 🌍إدارة المنتجات في الأسواق المتعددة
statement: 🌍إدارة المنتجات في الأسواق المتعددة إذا كانت ميزة الأسواق المتعددة مفعّلة في متجرك، يضيف لك الجدول عمود (عرض المنتج في الأسواق) الذي يوضح الأسواق التي يظهر فيها كل منتج (مثل السعودية والإمارات)، مع إمكانية التحكم في هذا الظهور مباشرة من الجدول.

identifier: 🌍إدارة المنتجات في الأسواق المتعددة
statement: كما يضيف الجدول أعمدة تسعير مستقلة لكل سوق تشمل: السعر، والتكلفة، والتخفيض وتواريخه الخاصة بذلك السوق، بحيث تدير سعر المنتج في كل سوق على حدة من نفس الصف.

identifier: 🚀 عند تفعيل الأسواق المتعددة:
statement: 🚀 عند تفعيل الأسواق المتعددة: توجد طريقتان لتعديل ترتيب المنتجات في الأسواق المتعددة: - موحّدة: تتيح لك تنظيم المنتجات داخل التصنيف، ويُطبَّق هذا الترتيب وأي تعديل عليه تلقائيًا على جميع الأسواق. - مخصّصة: يمنحك مرونة كاملة في التحكم بترتيب المنتجات داخل التصنيف لكل سوق على حدة.

identifier: التذكير بالسلة المتروكة بدون إرسال خصم
statement: ويمكنك اختيار سوق محدد لتطبيق التذكير عليه فقط، أو اختيار كل الأسواق ليشمل التذكير جميع أسواق المتجر. ملاحظة: خيار تحديد السوق يظهر فقط للتجار الذين قاموا بتفعيل ميزة الأسواق المتعددة. أما المتاجر التي لا تستخدم هذه الميزة، فسيظهر لها التذكير على المتجر بالكامل بدون تحديد سوق معيّن.

identifier: عروض السلة
statement: في حال تم تفعيل ميزة (الأسواق المتعددة) ستتمكن من تحديد السوق الذي سيتم تطبيق العرض عليه: 1- كل الأسواق: يتم تطبيق العرض على جميع الأسواق المفعلة بالمتجر، وتُعرض القيم بعملة المتجر الأساسية، مع تحويل تلقائي للقيم عند تغيير عملة المتجر إلى عملة أخرى. 2- سوق محدد: يتم تطبيق العرض على سوق معين فقط، وتُعتمد عملة هذا السوق في جميع القيم مثل قيمة مشتريات السلة، والحد الأقصى للخصم، وخصم المبلغ الثابت.

identifier: كيف يظهر حساب العميل داخل متجرك وما الذي يمكنه إدارته؟
statement: في حال تفعيل الأسواق المتعددة، سيختلف سجل البحث حسب السوق، بحيث يكون لكل سوق سجل بحث مستقل، وتتغير نتائج السجل عند انتقال العميل بين الأسواق.

identifier: مركز الإعدادات الموحد
statement: الأسواق المتعددة تتيح لك صفحة الأسواق المتعددة إدارة أسواق متجرك في عدة دول، مع التحكم في طريقة عرض المتجر، وتسعير المنتجات، وتحديد إتاحة الشراء والضرائب لكل سوق بما يتناسب مع دولته.

identifier: Shopper help hub: your guide to buying from Salla stores
statement: Salla is a Saudi technology platform that thousands of merchants use to build and run their online stores. As a shopper, you buy from the store itself, not from Salla.

identifier: Shopper help hub: your guide to buying from Salla stores
statement: The store you bought from is a legally independent business . It owns the product, sets the price and the return policy, prepares and ships your order, and handles customer service.

identifier: ❓ Did Salla sell me the product?
statement: No. The seller is the store where you placed the order, and it is the party responsible for the product, the shipping, and the return. Salla's role is limited to providing the technical platform the store runs on.

identifier: ❓ Can I buy from Salla stores from outside Saudi Arabia?
statement: That depends on the store. Each store decides which countries it ships to and which payment methods it accepts. Check the store's shipping policy page before you complete your order.

identifier: خاصية الأسواق
statement: تتيح خاصية الأسواق للتاجر إدارة أسعار المنتجات وتوفّرها حسب كل سوق جغرافي بشكل مستقل.

identifier: سعر مخصص لكل سوق وقناة
statement: حيث يمكن تحديد سعر مخصص لكل سوق وقناة وبعملة السوق نفسها، دون الاعتماد على سعر عالمي واحد أو التحويل التلقائي للعملات.

identifier: أيقونة الإجراءات > الإجراءات الخاصة بالسوق
statement: في الإجراءات الخاصة بالسوق ستتمكن من : إضافة منتج تخصيص الثيم

identifier: إدارة السوق > تفاصيل السوق
statement: بعد ذلك، أدخل تفاصيل السوق المطلوبة، والتي تشمل: اسم السوق (باللغة العربية)، وفي حال تفعيل اللغة الإنجليزية ستتمكن من إدخال اسم السوق باللغة الإنجليزية أيضًا. الدول المرتبطة بالسوق. عملة السوق.

identifier: عملة السوق
statement: عملة السوق: حدّد العملة التي سيتم اعتمادها لعرض أسعار المنتجات داخل هذا السوق.

identifier: خطوات إنشاء السوق > 2. إضافة المنتجات
statement: في خطوة إضافة المنتجات ، قم بإدخال المنتجات التي ترغب بإضافتها للسوق عن طريق الضغط على ايقونة إضافة منتجات

identifier: خطوات إنشاء السوق > 2. إعداد الأسعار > حدد طريقة إعداد السعر
statement: حدد طريقة إعداد السعر نسخ الأسعار من السوق الرئيسي كما هي مع استخدام عملة السوق الجديدة تحويل الأسعار تلقائيًا باستخدام سعر الصرف الحالي بين عملة السوق الرئيسي وعملة السوق الجديدة سأقوم بإدخال السعر يدويًا

identifier: خطوات إنشاء السوق > 4. إدارة الأسعار
statement: سيظهر لك ملخص السعر بشكل عام وفي حال رغبت بتخصيص سعر التخفيض للسوق قم بالضغط على ايقونة تعديل الأسعار

identifier: تخصيص الثيم لكل سوق
statement: يمكنك تخصيص ثيم لكل سوق بشكل مستقل و تخصيص البنرات، والأقسام، والمنتجات المعروضة، والعروض الترويجية لكل سوق على حدة، دون التأثير على بقية الأسواق.

identifier: تخصيص الثيم لكل سوق > نشر
statement: عند الإنتهاء من التخصيص يرجى الضغط على أيقونة( نشر ) ، بعد ذلك سيظهر للعميل التخصيص المتاح على حسب دولته

identifier: لوحة التحكم > الاعدادات > اللغات والعملات
statement: لتفعيل العملة الرئيسية للمتجر أو إضافة عملات أخرى من خلال: لوحة التحكم > الاعدادات > اللغات والعملات

identifier: العملات > العملة الأساسية للمتجر
statement: قم باختيار و تفعيل العملة الأساسية للمتجر بناء على عملة دولتك ، وفي حال أردت إضافة مزيد من العملات الأخرى قم بتفعيلها بالضغط على أيقونة تفعيل وبإمكانك تحديد العملة الأساسية بالمتجر من خلال الضغط على أيقونة اختيار كعملة أساسية.

identifier: العملة الأساسية
statement: العملة الأساسية هي العملة التي تم إدخال أسعار المنتجات باستخدامها، عند التعديل يرجى مراعاة القيام بتعديل أسعار جميع المنتجات للعملة الأساسية الجديدة.

identifier: تفعيل عملة دولة
statement: عند تفعيل عملة دولة يتم تفعيل الشحن إليها.

identifier: سعر الصرف عند تغيير العملة
statement: عند تغيير العملة سيتم تحويل أسعار المنتجات إلى العملة الجديدة بناءً على سعر الصرف في وقت التغيير، ونتيجة لذلك قد يحصل تغيير في مجموع المبيعات.

identifier: الدفع بالعملة الأساسية
statement: في حال تم تفعيل المدفوعات لزد [ مدفوعات زد متاحة لتجار السعودية و الكويت] كخيار دفع إلكتروني وتم تفعيل عملات أخرى غير العملة الأساسية (الريال السعودي \ الدينار الكويتي) بالمتجر ، سيتم استعراض أسعار المنتجات بالعملة المختارة مثل الريال العماني من قبل العميل لكن في مرحلة الدفع النهائي سيتم الدفع بالعملة الأساسية للمتجر (الريال السعودي\ الدينار الكويتي) لجميع الشبكات ما عدا “كي نت” سيتم الدفع بالدينار الكويتي.

identifier: اللغات والعملات > ملاحظة (help.zid.sa/store-language)
statement: في حال تم تفعيل المدفوعات لزد [ مدفوعات زد متاحة لتجار السعودية و الكويت] كخيار دفع إلكتروني وتم تفعيل عملات أخرى غير العملة الأساسية (الريال السعودي \ الدينار الكويتي) بالمتجر ، سيتم استعراض أسعار المنتجات بالعملة المختارة مثل الريال العماني من قبل العميل لكن في مرحلة الدفع النهائي سيتم الدفع بالعملة الأساسية للمتجر (الريال السعودي\ الدينار الكويتي) لجميع الشبكات ما عدا “كي نت” سيتم الدفع بالدينار الكويتي.

identifier: لغة وعملات المتجر
statement: إن توفير أكثر من لغة و عملة في المتجر الالكتروني يعتبر فرصة ممتازة لزيادة أرباحك و رفع مبيعاتك و يسهل الوصول إلى قدر أكبر من العملاء ويساعد في الانتشار و تحسين ظهور متجرك في محركات البحث.

identifier: سعر الصرف لبوابة الدفع
statement: المبلغ المدفوع خاضع لتحويل سعر الصرف لبوابة الدفع المفعلة.
