identifier: Configuring Offline Payment Methods: Available Countries
statement: Available Countries — Check the box for the countries where this payment method is available at checkout.
scope: the countries the merchant checks for each offline payment method

identifier: /developer/api-reference/rest/admin/management/shipping
statement: Manage shipping zones, shipping methods, and shipping carrier connections.

identifier: shipping zones
statement: You can configure shipping zones in the control panel or use the API to designate where a merchant ships their products and with which shipping methods should be available in each geographic region.

identifier: /developer/api-reference/rest/admin/management/tax
statement: Manage tax configuration for your store, including tax classes, tax properties, tax zones, tax rates, and tax settings. Use these APIs to classify products and customers for tax purposes, define geographic tax zones with rate schedules, and configure tax calculation behavior.

identifier: should_use_geolocation_to_determine_guest_shopper_tax_zone
statement: This setting determines which tax zone a store uses to estimate tax for guest shoppers.

identifier: Tax Settings API
statement: The Tax Settings API supports cross-border transactions. You can localize storefront prices for shoppers from different regions.

identifier: Settings > Setup > Tax
statement: Before you can provide tax estimates, the merchant must choose which regions they want you to service.

identifier: Settings APIs: global and channel-specific contextual overrides
statement: They can be configured both on the **global** level and as channel-specific **contextual overrides** that apply to only one sales channel.

identifier: channel-specific settings
statement: Each new channel will use the store's global default values unless the merchant chooses to override them by defining **channel-specific** settings.

identifier: global default
statement: When these merchants configure their store settings, they're modifying the global default versions of their settings.

identifier: Global-only settings: store_address_type, store_country
statement: Currently, the following settings are inherently global and cannot be modified with channel-specific overrides: > > * store\_address\_type > * store\_country

identifier: PUT /v3/settings/...
statement: You can modify global and channel-specific settings alike by sending `PUT` requests to the relevant endpoints.

identifier: The cumulative effect of global and channel-specific settings
statement: At every point of contact a shopper has with a storefront or other sales channel, channel-specific settings are displayed first. Global default settings will only appear to shoppers when channel-specific values for those properties are not defined.

identifier: GET /v3/settings/store/profile?channel_id=124
statement: Because channel-specific values exist for all store profile object properties, this channel is configured to override all the global default store profile configuration settings.

identifier: Localization settings (per storefront)
statement: Localization settings can be customized on each storefront to set the country, language, physical dimensions, date, and timezone. This allows your storefront to present itself as a domestic store based in the country that you are planning to sell to.

identifier: selected country
statement: Note: The selected country determines tax and shipping zone settings. This functionality is still in development for International Enhancements for Multi-Storefront.

identifier: Store profile settings (per storefront)
statement: Store profile settings can be localized on each of the storefronts to include a localized storefront shopper-facing store name, address, email, and phone number.

identifier: default shopper-facing language
statement: When a new storefront is created, you will be able to select a default shopper-facing language for that storefront.

identifier: default currency (per storefront)
statement: You can set the default currency for each storefront from the list of enabled currencies on your store, which is displayed to shoppers whenever they visit a given storefront.

identifier: Channel Manager › Domains
statement: You can connect a localized domain (such as “cats.fr”) or subdomain (such as “fr.cats.com”) to a storefront by navigating to the storefront in Channel Manager, and selecting Domains in the side navigation.

identifier: channel-specific price list
statement: By creating a channel-specific price list, you can set different prices in the same currency per different storefronts.

identifier: localized promotions
statement: You can create localized promotions for each storefront by assigning the promotion to only selected storefront channels and customizing the shopper-facing content within the promotion to match the storefront’s language.

identifier: settings per storefronts
statement: Merchants selling in different regions need to be able to customize settings per storefronts in order to provide shoppers with local units of measurement, currencies, and localized content.

identifier: International Enhancements for Multi-Storefront: product attributes per locale
statement: To use these features, set product attributes to locales within storefront channels. This update overrides global product attributes.

identifier: GraphQL Admin API (International Enhancements for MSF)
statement: The catalog features in *International Enhancements for MSF* are part of the GraphQL Admin API. You can use this GraphQL management API to set and query catalog data for a locale *within a channel*.

identifier: Fastlane by PayPal: Requirements (shoppers)
statement: Fastlane by PayPal is only available for shoppers located in a supported country and using a supported currency.

identifier: FAQ: What countries are supported by Fastlane by PayPal?
statement: Fastlane by PayPal supports the following store, Braintree merchant account or PayPal business account, and shopper countries. Note that shoppers must also use a supported transactional currency. Andorra Finland Lichtenstein Romania Australia France Lithuania San Marino Austria Germany Luxembourg Singapore Canada Greece Malaysia Slovakia China Hong Kong Malta Slovenia Croatia Hungary Monaco Spain Cyprus Iceland Netherlands United Kingdom Czechia Ireland New Zealand United States Denmark Italy Norway Estonia Latvia Portugal

identifier: tax zones
statement: To charge different rates for different geographic locations, you will create one or more tax zones. A tax zone specifies the geographical area where a group of tax rates apply. Set whether the tax zone geographical area applies to a customer’s billing address, shipping or pickup address, or your store’s shipping origin address in your tax settings.

identifier: Zone type
statement: Zone type — how the zone is defined. Zones can be based on country, state, or postal code.

identifier: site
statement: A **site** is a website owned or controlled exclusively by the merchant, usually for hosting a storefront website. Every site will be tied to exactly one channel, but because not all sales channels are sites, channels are not required to have a site. Sites are mainly relevant to storefront-type channels, and they serve as containers for settings and objects that only apply to websites.

identifier: Multi-Storefront (MSF)
statement: Multi-Storefront (MSF) allows you to use a single BigCommerce “store” to power multiple “storefronts”. Each of these storefronts can have its own unique domain, theme, categories, web pages, social media links, price lists, email templates, and more. The settings and data for each of these storefronts are managed from one BigCommerce control panel.

identifier: Multi-Storefront: global store functions
statement: Depending on your business model, multi-storefront may work for some merchants as a multi-region or cross-border solution. However, some store functions are global and are shared across storefronts, such as the built-in blog. Additionally, even though the same product can be assigned to different storefronts, product attributes (like description and name) cannot be overridden into a different language without customization. Stores on a Performance plan will have access to additional product localization fields.

identifier: Features: multiple native storefronts
statement: With multiple native storefronts, you can do all of this within the control panel: Create and manage multiple BigCommerce storefronts within a single control panel. Configure storefront settings and internal notifications for each storefront. Connect different domain names and SSL certificates for each storefront. Apply and customize themes, page templates, email templates, widgets, web pages, scripts, and social media links for each storefront. Set and manage default storefront currency and unique sets of currencies per storefront. Configure unique checkout settings per storefront. Set up web analytics (like Google Analytics) specific to each storefront. Set up a Meta Pixel specific to each storefront. Create storefront-unique categories and make products available on one or multiple storefronts. Stores on a Performance plan will have access to additional product localization fields. Configure inventory settings for each storefront, including notifications. Control product filtering settings per storefront and per category. Configure category and web page URL structure per storefront. Use Price Lists for custom pricing on each storefront. View and manage orders and customers for multiple storefronts in one place. Control product purchasability per storefront. Create Automatic and Coupon Promotions per storefront (using the Standard Promotions editor). Manage customer groups (like retail or wholesale) for each storefront and set the default group. Create category-level discounts per storefront for specific customer groups. Create customers and manage login access to each storefront. Control storefront status for all storefronts from Channel Manager. Filter ecommerce sales reports by native storefront channel. Collect and export newsletter subscriptions per storefront. Create and manage 301 redirects per storefront. Manage shipping methods and out of delivery zone messaging per storefront.

identifier: Features: multiple headless storefronts
statement: With multiple headless storefronts, you can do all of this within the control panel: Create and manage multiple headless storefronts within a single control panel. Configure storefront settings for each storefront. Connect different domain names and SSL certificates for each storefront (this is managed outside of BigCommerce for headless storefronts). Create storefront-unique categories and make products available on one or multiple storefronts. Stores on a Performance plan will have access to additional product localization fields. Configure category and web page URL structure per storefront. Enable, disable, and customize transactional store emails and abandoned cart notifications. Configure inventory settings for each storefront, including notifications. Configure unique checkout settings per storefront when using redirected checkout. Use price lists for custom pricing on each storefront. Set up analytics tracking for each headless storefront. Create Automatic and Coupon Promotions per storefront (using the Standard Promotions editor). Set category-level discounts per storefront and customer group with appropriate prices reflected on the storefront. Enable/disable purchasing on the storefront. Control storefront status for all storefronts from Channel Manager. Create customers and manage login access to each storefront. Filter ecommerce sales reports by headless storefront channel. Create and manage 301 redirects per storefront. Manage shipping methods and out of delivery zone messaging per storefront.

identifier: Multi-Storefront features: API
statement: All of these features are available via the API as well. See Introduction to Multi-Storefront in the Dev Center.

identifier: App Support
statement: All apps are designed to work at a store level and are installed at the store level. Every app should work on the default storefront that is provisioned when a new store is created.

identifier: Settings › Account sign up form › Address Fields
statement: On the Address Fields tab, you can manage the address fields that appear on account registration, customer account, and checkout pages. The same form fields are used for both the billing and shipping address, though the data your customers provide for each can be different from one another.

identifier: Address Fields: built-in required address fields
statement: There are seven built-in required address fields: First Name Last Name Address Line 1 Suburb/City Country State/Province Zip/Postcode

identifier: Address Fields: additional built-in fields
statement: There are three additional built-in fields, but they are not required by default: Phone Number* Company Name Address Line 2

identifier: Address Fields: built-in fields
statement: These fields cannot be removed, but can be renamed. The new names will be reflected on the account registration page and the customer Address Book, but not checkout.

identifier: Address Fields: Required setting
statement: Only the “Required” setting for Phone Number, Company Name, and Address Line 2 built-in fields can be adjusted for the Account Settings, registration, and checkout pages. All other built-in fields are required for shipping and checkout functionality and cannot be made optional.

identifier: Simple shipping address entry: country drop-down
statement: The default country in the drop-down menu is based on the customer’s IP address. Additionally, the menu only includes countries which have been set up in the Shipping page if configured.

identifier: Phone Number field: number validation
statement: When enabled, the built-in Phone Number field has different restrictions while and also performing number validation: Only the + special character is allowed and only as the first character for entering a country code. Only numbers are accepted. The amount of entered numbers must be valid for the country on the address. Spaces and dashes are ignored.

identifier: Google Address Autocomplete
statement: Enabling Google Address Autocomplete allows customers in select countries to check out faster by providing a list of potential matching addresses as the customer enters their billing or shipping address.

identifier: Enhanced checkout experience: address sections
statement: The country field is featured at the top of address sections as it provides context to the other fields. The remainder of fields are displayed in the order they are configured in your store’s settings.
scope: the enhanced checkout experience (Enable enhanced checkout experience checked)

identifier: Catalyst Multi-Storefront Overview
statement: How Catalyst supports selling internationally with multiple channels, each with its own language, currency, and locale-specific URLs.

identifier: Catalyst: selling internationally to multiple countries; Multi-Storefront (MSF) setup
statement: Catalyst supports selling internationally to multiple countries, where each country has its own language, currency, payment methods, and so on. This requires a Multi-Storefront (MSF) setup.

identifier: Storefront content: Channel Manager
statement: In a multi-storefront setup, you can manage localization settings and content for each storefront in the control panel using the [Channel Manager](https://support.bigcommerce.com/s/article/Selling-Everywhere-with-Channel-Manager).

identifier: Storefront content (multi-storefront setup): The storefront content to localize includes the following
statement: The storefront content to localize includes the following: * [Products and categories](https://support.bigcommerce.com/s/article/Getting-Started-with-Localization-on-Multi-Storefronts?language=en_US#localizing-products)

identifier: Storefront content (multi-storefront setup): The storefront content to localize includes the following
statement: * [Currency](https://support.bigcommerce.com/s/article/Getting-Started-with-Localization-on-Multi-Storefronts?language=en_US#currency) * [Pricing via price lists](https://support.bigcommerce.com/s/article/Getting-Started-with-Localization-on-Multi-Storefronts?language=en_US#localizing-products)

identifier: Storefront content (multi-storefront setup): The storefront content to localize includes the following
statement: * [Date and physical dimension formats](https://support.bigcommerce.com/s/article/Getting-Started-with-Localization-on-Multi-Storefronts?language=en_US#localizing-settings) * Checkout * Order statuses

identifier: Storefront content (multi-storefront setup): The storefront content to localize includes the following
statement: * [Promotions](https://support.bigcommerce.com/s/article/Getting-Started-with-Localization-on-Multi-Storefronts?language=en_US#promotions-comms) * [Emails](https://support.bigcommerce.com/s/article/Getting-Started-with-Localization-on-Multi-Storefronts?language=en_US#promotions-comms)

identifier: Storefront content (multi-storefront setup): The storefront content to localize includes the following
statement: * Payment methods * Shipping options * Tax settings

identifier: Locale-specific URLs: multiple languages through channels
statement: Catalyst can service multiple languages by connecting multiple channels to the storefronts and routing each language through different subpaths.

identifier: Locale-specific URLs: Root domain, subdomain, or gTLD
statement: | Root domain, subdomain, or gTLD | `store.com`, `fr.store.com`, or `store.co.uk` | International selling, where you want to personalize the language, currency, payment methods, and more. | Create a [storefront channel](/developer/docs/admin/multi-storefront) and point it to a domain, subdomain, or gTLD. |

identifier: Locale-specific URLs: Domain subpath
statement: | Domain subpath | `store.com/fr` | Providing multiple languages within a country. | Each locale's subfolder is set in the control panel on your default channel. The locale can load data from a different channel through `channels.config.ts`. |

identifier: Catalyst Multi-Storefront Setup
statement: Set up a Catalyst storefront that serves multiple countries and locales from one app by mapping locales to BigCommerce channels.

identifier: Dynamic data: Channel data
statement: *Channel data* - Many of the features that you localize, like catalog and pricing, are first created for your global store and then assigned to storefront channels. You can then assign the storefront channel to a locale in the Catalyst app so that channel-specific data gets propagated to those locales.

identifier: Dynamic data: Global data
statement: *Global data* - Other features, like tax, belong to the global store and require that you create zones, or regions, where you want tax rules to apply.

identifier: Configure channels in your Catalyst app: a locale per storefront; region subtag
statement: You can assign a given locale to only one storefront, so two storefronts can't share a locale. However, for some locales, you can add a subtag to the locale code to indicate the region, for example, `en-US` (U.S. English) and `en-AU` (Australian English).

identifier: Dynamic data: Catalog: products per channel
statement: To sell different products in the US and Switzerland, you need to assign US products to the US channel and Swiss products to the other channel.
scope: the tutorial's US and Swiss channels

identifier: Currencies: Visible in the global settings
statement: Currencies must be **Visible** on the storefront in the global settings to show up in Catalyst.

identifier: Currencies: assign the currency to a channel
statement: Assign the currency to the correct channel by clicking the channels dropdown next to the currency.

identifier: Carts API: locale-based overrides
statement: The Carts API supports selling in different markets by allowing locale-based overrides for product details. Supply a cart's locale and add `option_selections` to the cart's line items to configure alternative product names, option names, and modifier values.

identifier: Carts API: Locale format
statement: The locale field supports language, script, and region codes in the [ISO-639 standard](https://www.iso.org/iso-639-language-codes.html) format.

identifier: Buy Online, Pick up in Store: Multi-channel awareness
statement: *Buy Online, Pick up in Store* currently supports pick up on a single storefront channel. Currently, you cannot have different warehouse locations and inventory service different storefront channels.
scope: Buy Online, Pick up in Store

identifier: Channel Webhooks: Settings (store/channel/{channel_id}/settings/ events)
statement: The following settings webhook events fire in response to actions that affect a specific channel on a store:

identifier: Channel Webhooks: Settings (store/channel/{channel_id}/settings/ events)
statement: | `store/channel/{channel_id}/settings/*` | Fires when subscribed to all settings updates for the specified channel. | | `store/channel/{channel_id}/settings/currency/updated` | Fires when currency associated with the specified channel is updated. |

identifier: Channel Webhooks: Settings (store/channel/{channel_id}/settings/ events)
statement: | `store/channel/{channel_id}/settings/profile/updated` | Fires when any of the global store profile settings are updated. Fires for both channel-specific profile settings changes and for changes to any global defaults that the specified channel inherits.

identifier: Channel Webhooks: Settings (store/channel/{channel_id}/settings/ events)
statement: | `store/channel/{channel_id}/settings/locale/updated` | Fires when a locale is updated for any channel. The corresponding endpoint is [Update a locale](/developer/docs/admin/store-configuration/settings/locales-configuration#update-a-locale). |

identifier: Channel Webhooks: Settings (store/channel/{channel_id}/settings/ events)
statement: | `store/channel/{channel_id}/settings/locale/deleted` | Fires when a locale is deleted from any channel. The corresponding endpoint is [Delete a locale](/developer/docs/admin/store-configuration/settings/locales-configuration#delete-a-locale). |

identifier: Channel Webhooks: Settings (store/channel/{channel_id}/settings/ events)
statement: | `store/channel/{channel_id}/settings/logo/updated` | Fires when any of the global logo settings are updated. The corresponding endpoint is [Update store logo settings](/developer/api-reference/rest/admin/management/settings/logo/update-settings-logo). |

identifier: Channel Webhooks: Settings (store/channel/{channel_id}/settings/ events)
statement: | `store/channel/{channel_id}/settings/logo/image/updated` | Fires when any of the logo image settings that apply to the specified channel are updated. |

identifier: Channel Webhooks: Settings (store/channel/{channel_id}/settings/ events)
statement: | `store/channel/{channel_id}/settings/favicon/image/updated` | Fires when any of the favicon image settings that apply to the specified channel are updated. |

identifier: Channel Webhooks: Settings (store/channel/{channel_id}/settings/ events)
statement: | `store/channel/{channel_id}/settings/checkout/updated` | Fires when checkout settings that affect a specified channel are updated. The corresponding endpoint is [Update channel cart settings](/developer/api-reference/rest/admin/management/carts/settings/update-channel-cart-settings). |

identifier: Channel Webhooks: Settings (store/channel/{channel_id}/settings/ events)
statement: | `store/channel/{channel_id}/settings/seo/updated` | Fires when SEO settings that affect the specified channel are updated. The corresponding endpoint is [Update storefront SEO settings](/developer/api-reference/rest/admin/management/settings/storefront-seo/update-settings-storefront-seo). |

identifier: Channel Webhooks: Settings (store/channel/{channel_id}/settings/ events)
statement: | `store/channel/{channel_id}/settings/search/updated` | Fires when storefront search settings that affect the specified channel are updated.

identifier: Channel Webhooks: Settings (store/channel/{channel_id}/settings/ events)
statement: | `store/channel/{channel_id}/settings/inventory/updated` | Fires when inventory settings that affect the specified channel are updated. The corresponding endpoint is [Update inventory settings](/developer/api-reference/rest/admin/management/settings/inventory/update-settings-inventory). |

identifier: Channel Webhooks: Settings (store/channel/{channel_id}/settings/ events)
statement: | `store/channel/{channel_id}/settings/robots/updated` | Fires when search engine robot settings that affect the specified channel are updated.

identifier: Channel Webhooks: Settings (store/channel/{channel_id}/settings/ events)
statement: | `store/channel/{channel_id}/settings/category/updated` | Fires when category settings that affect the specified channel are updated.

identifier: Channel Webhooks: Settings (store/channel/{channel_id}/settings/ events)
statement: | `store/channel/{channel_id}/settings/product/updated` | Fires when product settings that affect the specified channel are updated.

identifier: Channel Webhooks: Settings (store/channel/{channel_id}/settings/ events)
statement: | `store/channel/{channel_id}/settings/catalog/updated` | Fires when catalog settings that affect the specified channel are updated. The corresponding endpoint is [Update catalog settings](/developer/api-reference/rest/admin/management/settings/catalog/update-settings-catalog). |

identifier: Channel Webhooks: Settings (store/channel/{channel_id}/settings/ events)
statement: | `store/channel/{channel_id}/settings/security/updated` | Fires when security settings that affect the specified channel are updated.

identifier: Channel Webhooks: Settings (store/channel/{channel_id}/settings/ events)
statement: | `store/channel/{channel_id}/settings/searchContextFilters/updated` | Fires when search context filters that affect the specified channel are updated.

identifier: Channel Webhooks: Settings (store/channel/{channel_id}/settings/ events)
statement: | `store/channel/{channel_id}/settings/customer/updated` | Fires when customer settings that affect the specified channel are updated, including privacy settings and the channel's default customer group.

identifier: PUT https://api.bigcommerce.com/stores/{store_hash}/v3/settings/store/profile (Update Store Profile Settings): channel_id
statement: Channel ID can be used as a query parameter for updating channel-specific settings. If omitted, you will interact with the global settings only.

identifier: GET https://api.bigcommerce.com/stores/{store_hash}/v2/store (Get Store Information)
statement: Returns metadata about the global settings for a store. Some of these values are independently configurable on a per-storefront or per-channel basis.

identifier: Connecting with Stripe OCS: Stripe Adaptive Pricing: payouts
statement: With Stripe Adaptive Pricing, shoppers can complete orders in their local currency, while payouts to your account are settled in your default currency.

identifier: Managing Currencies: FAQ: storefront-specific default currency (Channel Manager, Set as Channel default currency)
statement: To assign a storefront-specific default currency, go to Channel Manager and click a storefront name to access its settings page. In Currencies, click on the Action menu and select Set as Channel default currency.

identifier: Automatic Tax Setup: Provider Targeting (Settings › Tax, Country and Subdivisions)
statement: After you have enabled an automatic tax provider, you will need to configure its Provider Targeting settings to only include the countries and subdivisions (such as states or provinces) you want the provider to calculate tax for. Basic Tax is then used for all regions that are not targeted by the provider.

identifier: Automatic Tax Setup: FAQ: Can I show prices inclusive of tax to some countries and exclusive of tax for others?
statement: Yes, you can set this up using the price display settings in your tax zones. Although tax zone display is configured in Basic Tax settings, it will also apply to your automatic tax provider when enabled.

identifier: Localization Settings: Default Country
statement: The default country setting determines which payment methods are available to be set up on your store. The selected country also allows you to quickly adjust standard dimension and date and time formats.

identifier: Localization Settings: Requirements: Manage Settings permission (languages)
statement: To view and manage languages, the Manage Settings permission must be enabled on your user account.

identifier: Localization Settings: FAQ: I have more than one storefront, can I configure channel-specific localization settings?
statement: For additional storefronts, you can use the store’s global settings or configure the default country, physical dimensions, and date and timezone settings separately per channel.

identifier: Localization Settings: FAQ: channel-specific localization settings (Edit channel; Edit Channels permission)
statement: Under the Storefront Languages section in Settings › Localization, click the Action menu (⋯) next to the desired channel, then select Edit channel from the drop-down list. Note that in addition to the general requirements, you must also have the Edit Channels permission enabled.

identifier: Store Profile Settings: How It Works (Settings › Store profile; Storefront settings › Contact information)
statement: When you create a new store, the basic contact information you provide, such as the store name and email address, is added to the store profile. You can manage store information globally from Settings › Store profile, or you can add unique information to individual storefronts from Channels › Channel Manager by clicking the storefront’s name and going to Storefront settings › Contact information.

identifier: User Roles and Permissions: High-Risk Permissions: Edit Channels
statement: Edit Channels Edit channel settings and additional storefronts in the Channel Manager. This permission and Store Design are required to access the Theme Marketplace and the Edit Theme Files action in Page Builder for multi-storefront stores.

identifier: Localization Settings: Physical Dimensions; Date and Timezone: Set standard formats for [country]
statement: To reset values to the standard formats for your store’s default country, click Set standard formats for [country].

identifier: Localization Settings: Storefront Languages (Edit languages)
statement: Each channel can support up to five languages. To add new languages, change your default language, and manage translations, click the Action menu (⋯) and select Edit languages.

identifier: Localization Settings: FAQ: Which payment gateways support automatic translation? (PayPal)
statement: In addition to the payment methods automatically translated by BigCommerce, PayPal automatically translates many of its payment methods based on the shopper’s location, rather than the selected language.

identifier: Store Profile Settings: FAQ: Which countries support seamless translation in the storefront?
statement: If you create a new store based in one of the following countries, the store's content will be in your country's native language by default. All other countries and languages require theme lang file customization.

identifier: Store Profile Settings: FAQ: Which countries support seamless translation in the storefront? (list)
statement: Danish / Dansk (da) Dutch; Flemish / Nederlands (nl) English (en) French / Français (fr) French; Belgium / Français de Belgique (fr-BE) French; Canada / Français de Canada (fr-CA) German / Deutsch (de) Italian / Italiano (it) Japanese / 日本語 (ja) Polish (pl) Portuguese / Português (pt)

identifier: Store Profile Settings: FAQ: Which countries support seamless translation in the storefront? (list)
statement: Spanish; Castilian / Español/Castellano (es) Spanish Latin America / Español Latinoamérica (es-419) Spanish; Argentina / Español rioplatense (es-AR) Spanish; Chile / Español chileno (es-CL) Spanish; Colombia / Español colombiano (es-CO) Spanish Costa Rica (es-CR)

identifier: Store Profile Settings: FAQ: Which countries support seamless translation in the storefront? (list)
statement: Spanish; Mexico / Español mexicano (es-MX) Spanish; Peru / Español peruano (es-PE) Swedish / Svenska (sv)

identifier: Physical Dimension Settings and the Shipping Calculator: FAQ: Can I apply physical dimension settings on a per-product basis?
statement: No, settings like measurement units and factoring dimension are applied globally. However, you can include measurements in different units within a product’s description.

identifier: Invoices: Customizing the Invoice Email (Marketing › Transactional Emails; Global (storefront defaults))
statement: If you have more than one storefront, you can customize each storefront’s templates independently by selecting the desired storefront from the drop-down menu at the top of the page. If you want to customize all storefront templates or have a single-storefront store, leave the menu selection on Global (storefront defaults).

identifier: Translations for Address Form Fields (resourceType ADDRESS_FORM_FIELDS)
statement: The following entities are translatable for address form fields: * Label as `label` - The display label for the form field * Option values as `option_{base64string}` - Option values where the base64 string encodes the original option text

identifier: Translations for Address Form Fields: Query a List of Translations
statement: This query returns a paginated list of translations by resourceType, channel, and locale with a maximum of 50 results per request.

identifier: Translations Admin GraphQL API: Note (non-default channel locale)
statement: Translation API allows users to add content translations to any non-default channel locale. In order to update content on a default channel language, please use respective management API.

identifier: Translations Admin GraphQL API: How does this API work? Core Concepts
statement: When using the GraphQL Admin API to manage translations, the following fields are used to identify the relevant channel, locale, and resource so that all data is assigned properly.

identifier: Enabling Multi-Language Checkout: Localized country and state names
statement: BigCommerce's Optimized One-Page Checkout will translate displayed **Country/State** names into supported languages. To take advantage of this functionality, enable Optimized One-Page Checkout on your store. You do not need to provide any keys-values for the **Country/State** names already translated within the BigCommerce platform. As with the translation options described above, the storefront will automatically display the translated **Country/State** names based on the default storefront language defined in the control panel.

identifier: Google Autocomplete for Addresses
statement: Free for up to 10,000 monthly events, merchants in any location can set up and enable Google Autocomplete for addresses. Customer addresses in Australia, Canada, New Zealand, the United Kingdom, and the United States are supported.

identifier: Google Autocomplete for Addresses: How It Works (UK postcodes)
statement: Postcodes are not autofilled for UK addresses. To prevent incorrectly autofilled shipping and billing addresses, UK customers must manually enter their postcode.

identifier: Google Autocomplete for Addresses: BigCommerce Setup (Settings › Checkout › Optimized one-page checkout › Shipping)
statement: Check the box next to Use Google Maps services to autocomplete shipping and billing addresses, then enter the API key that you copied from your Google Cloud project.

identifier: Google Autocomplete for Addresses: Requirements: Manage Settings permission
statement: To manage your store’s checkout settings, you must have the Manage Settings permission enabled on your user account.

identifier: Storefront Checkout Configurations: FAQ: What checkout configurations are available for stores using Multi-Storefront?
statement: Stores with more than one storefront can use any of the checkout configurations listed above. In addition, several checkout settings can be configured uniquely per storefront.
scope: stores with more than one storefront

identifier: Checkout and Orders on Multi-Storefront: Checkout (Channel Manager › [storefront] › Checkout; Use global)
statement: Several checkout settings can be uniquely configured per storefront, allowing you to customize your checkout pages to support regional shopping experiences. Go to Channel Manager and select the storefront. Click Checkout in the side navigation. By default, your storefront uses your store’s checkout settings. When editing the checkout settings for a storefront, uncheck "Use global", then update the available settings for the storefront.

identifier: Configuring Storefronts: Storefront Overview: left side navigation: Checkout
statement: Checkout — includes checkout behavior for guest shoppers and existing customers, checkout type, privacy policy, terms and conditions, contact email on the order confirmation page, and custom checkout and order confirmation page URLs

identifier: Store Profile Settings: Contact Information (Settings › Store profile; Channels › Channel Manager › Storefront settings › Contact information)
statement: Go to Settings › Store profile to update or change your store's contact information. If you are using Multi-Storefront, go to Channels › Channel Manager, click on the name of your storefront, and navigate to Storefront settings › Contact information.

identifier: Store Profile Settings: Contact Information (fields)
statement: Store display name — The name of your store as you want it to appear in all emails, invoices, order confirmation page, the header of your store, and on your BigCommerce account.

identifier: Store Profile Settings: Contact Information (fields)
statement: Address — The physical address of your store or place of business; appears on printed invoices and in the footer of most themes.

identifier: Store Profile Settings: Contact Information (fields)
statement: Address type — Specifies whether the above address is a home or commercial office, retail store, or warehouse.

identifier: Store Profile Settings: Contact Information (fields)
statement: Email — The email address used by all emails sent by the store, such as invoices and order status updates.

identifier: Store Profile Settings: Contact Information (fields)
statement: Phone — The phone number as you wish it to appear on your storefront. If left blank, no phone number will appear.

identifier: Configuring Storefronts: Storefront Overview: left side navigation: Storefront settings
statement: Storefront settings — includes storefront status, contact information, logo and favicon, inventory rules, and many other common settings

identifier: Configuring Storefronts: Use global
statement: If Use global is checked, then the setting will use “global” storefront settings, which are configured outside of Channel Manager. For example, this storefront's contact information setting is using the data from Settings › Store profile.

identifier: Checkout and Orders on Multi-Storefront: Order Confirmation Settings: Contact Email
statement: Contact Email — Specify an email address to appear on the order confirmation ("Thanks for your order") page. By default, the order confirmation page displays the storewide order confirmation contact email address, or if that field is empty, the store administrator email address in your store's Miscellaneous settings.

identifier: Checkout Settings: Contact email
statement: The Contact Email field in your checkout settings allows you to specify an email address to appear on the order confirmation ("Thanks for your order") page. If you leave the Contact Email field blank, the order confirmation page displays the store administrator email address entered in your store's Miscellaneous settings.

identifier: Checkout Settings: Contact email (the order confirmation page's phone number)
statement: Want to change the phone number on the order confirmation page? This page uses the phone number listed in the store profile.

identifier: Customer Order Notifications: Reply-to Email Address
statement: The order confirmation email is sent from your store using the email address entered in your store profile contact information. If a customer replies to an order email message, this is the address it will attempt to deliver to.

identifier: Customer Order Notifications: Reply-to Email Address (Using Multi-Storefront?)
statement: Using Multi-Storefront? You can use the global setting or specify a store email address per storefront. See Single-Storefront vs. Multi-Storefront for other settings moved into Channel Manager.

identifier: International Enhancements for Multi-Storefront: Settings and launch
statement: Settings and launch — Configure key storefront settings, such as contact information, search settings, and customer privacy, and make the storefront available to shoppers.

identifier: Using Multiple Currencies: currency converter (a visitor's IP address)
statement: If you have multiple currencies enabled, a currency converter will display on your store that will allow customers to choose among the currencies you have set up. If a visitor's IP address matches a supported country, they will see the appropriate currency automatically.

identifier: Storefront selector for multi-storefront
statement: To localize shopping experiences, you can have multiple storefronts that target specific shopper segments, regions, or brands. You can add a selector to a theme so shoppers can select the storefront they want to browse from a list of options.

identifier: Storefront selector for multi-storefront: what you can do with the selectors
statement: You can do the following with the storefront selectors that you create and inject into a theme: * Customize the style of the switcher and its options. * Choose which pages you want the selector to appear. * Select the storefronts that you include in the selector.

identifier: Storefront selector for multi-storefront: Steps to add storefront selector data (config.json, theme_settings)
statement: Currently, there is no Stencil object for the storefront selector. Instead, you can add data for the storefront selector in the `config.json` file, which allows the selector to appear in the `theme_settings` Stencil object.

identifier: Catalyst Multi-Storefront Setup: Configure channels in your Catalyst app (language selector)
statement: In your Catalyst app, configure which channel each locale pulls data from. When a shopper switches to a locale in the language selector, that channel's data is shown.

identifier: Customers and Multi-Storefront: Customer Accounts
statement: When a shopper creates a customer account, that account can only access the storefront on which it was created. The same login information will not work on your other native storefronts. This is the default behavior for Multi-Storefront (MSF) customer accounts, but it can be modified to allow customers to access all storefronts connected to your store. See Allowing Global Logins for more information.

identifier: Customers and Multi-Storefront: Allowing Global Logins (origin channel)
statement: A customer’s access to storefronts outside of their origin channel is based on the Allow global logins setting for that channel. All channels can manage their settings separately in the control panel.

identifier: Customers and Multi-Storefront: Allowing Global Logins (allow_global_login)
statement: When allow_global_login is set to true (default behavior) or Allow global logins is checked, customers created on any additional native and headless storefronts can access that channel. Note that headless storefront customers need access to the default storefront for checkout functionality.

identifier: Processing Returns: Return Settings (Settings › Returns)
statement: Return settings are located under Settings › Returns in the control panel.

identifier: Processing Returns: Return Settings: Yes, enable returns requests
statement: The returns system can be enabled by checking Yes, enable returns requests. Once activated, customers will be able to submit a return request from their account.

identifier: Processing Returns: Return Settings: Return Instructions
statement: The Return Instructions field can be used to provide direction after the request has been submitted. Use this to outline what customers can expect from you, or what the procedure is for a return or exchange.

identifier: Processing Returns: Return Settings: Return Reasons
statement: The Return Reasons field is where you provide your customers a list of acceptable reasons for returns.

identifier: Processing Returns: Return Settings: Return Actions
statement: The Return Actions field is where you can list the available resolution actions that a customer chooses from when submitting a return request.

identifier: Processing Returns: Return Settings: reset Return Reasons and Return Actions to their default values
statement: Check the box to reset the Return Reasons and Return Actions to their default values. This setting, once saved, will also automatically translate the default values to your store’s language.

identifier: Processing Returns: Requirements: Manage Settings and Manage Returns permissions
statement: To access Return Settings, the Manage Settings permission must be enabled on your user account. To process returns, the Manage Returns permission must be enabled on your user account.

identifier: Processing Returns: Creating a Returns Policy Page (Storefront › Web Pages)
statement: To create the page, go to Storefront › Web Pages. Follow the steps in Adding Web Pages and set the Page Name to “Shipping and Returns Policy” or something similar.

identifier: Getting Started with Localization on Multi-Storefronts: Return reasons and actions
statement: You can click to enable returns for your store. The default values for return reasons and actions will be automatically translated per storefront, based on the selected default language for the storefront. See Processing Returns for more information on using this feature.

identifier: Getting Started with Localization on Multi-Storefronts: Return reasons and actions (Watch out!)
statement: Watch out! Do not customize your store’s return reasons and actions, as this breaks the translation automation.

identifier: International Enhancements for Multi-Storefront: FAQ: Can return reasons and actions be localized per storefront?
statement: Yes, the default values for return reasons and actions will be automatically translated per storefront, based on the default language selected per given storefront If you have customized your reasons and actions, they will not be automatically translated. See Processing Returns for more information.

identifier: Team permissions
statement: Team permissions is BigCommerce's group-based access control system. It replaces per-user permission checkboxes with reusable **user groups**, predefined **policy** bundles, and per-store **targets**. A user's effective access is the union of every policy granted by every group they belong to.

identifier: Team permissions: How team permissions works (the three concepts)
statement: **User groups** — Named, reusable bundles of access. For example, *Warehouse*, *Sales Rep*, *Finance*.

identifier: Team permissions: How team permissions works (the three concepts)
statement: **Policies** — Predefined permission bundles such as *Orders Read* or *Account Users Manage*. Policies are granted to groups, not to individual users.

identifier: Team permissions: How team permissions works (the three concepts)
statement: **Targets** — The resource a policy applies to: a specific store, or the account itself.

identifier: Team permissions: Account Administrators group
statement: A default **Account Administrators** group is provisioned with each account and grants account-level access. Store owners and other account admins must remain members of this group to keep account-level permissions after team permissions is enabled.

identifier: User Roles and Permissions (introduction)
statement: A single store can have multiple users that log in to assist with the day-to-day functions of managing a store or performing a specific role in the business. Each user should have their own account, with permissions limited to only their areas of responsibility.

identifier: User Roles and Permissions: Editing user permissions (Settings › Users)
statement: To edit user permissions, go to Settings › Users while logged in as the store owner or a user account with the Manage Users and Edit Users permissions enabled. Click the Action button for the desired user account, then select Edit.

identifier: User Roles and Permissions: High-Risk Permissions: Create Channels
statement: Create Channels Add channels in the Channel Manager.

identifier: User Roles and Permissions: High-Risk Permissions: Delete Channels
statement: Delete Channels Delete channels from the Channel Manager.

identifier: Agentic checkout
statement: Enable transactions within AI-powered shopping experiences while remaining merchant of record.

identifier: Using the App Marketplace: Install applications permission
statement: To install or update apps and leave reviews, you must be the store owner or have the Install applications permission enabled on your user account.
scope: a store; the store owner or a user with the Install applications permission

identifier: Using the App Marketplace: Uninstall applications permission
statement: To uninstall apps or cancel an app installation, you must have the Uninstall applications permission enabled.
scope: a store; a user with the Uninstall applications permission

identifier: Using the App Marketplace: Launch applications permission
statement: To launch apps, you must be the store owner, have the Launch applications permission, or have been granted access to a multi-user Single Click App.
scope: a store; the store owner, a user with the Launch applications permission, or a user granted a multi-user Single Click App

identifier: Apps › My apps
statement: View a searchable list of your installed apps by going to Apps › My apps in the control panel. From the list, you can access app details, apply updates, and uninstall apps.

identifier: User permissions: Install applications
statement: Install applications Install apps from the App Marketplace.
scope: a user account of a store

identifier: User permissions: Uninstall applications
statement: Uninstall applications Uninstall apps from the store.
scope: a user account of a store

identifier: Single Click Apps: third-party sales channels
statement: Note that many third-party sales channels are apps, which can only be installed by the store owner or users with the Install applications permission.
scope: a store; the store owner or a user with the Install applications permission
